items.title: Namespace packages
items.text:
canVODpy uses Python 3.3+ implicit namespace packages to let eleven independent packages share the canvod.* import prefix: a unified API backed by separately installable wheels.

from canvod.readers import Rnxv3Obs
from canvod.auxiliary import Sp3File
from canvod.grids import EqualAreaBuilder
from canvod.store import MyIcechunkStore

items.title: How it works
items.text:
A namespace package is created by omitting __init__.py from the shared parent directory. Python treats a directory without __init__.py as a namespace that multiple packages can contribute to.

Namespace layoutRegular package (wrong)Combined site-packages 
canvod-readers/src/
  canvod/                  ← namespace directory, NO __init__.py
    readers/
      __init__.py          ← regular package starts here
      base.py

canvod-auxiliary/src/
  canvod/                  ← same namespace, different package
    auxiliary/
      __init__.py

src/
  canvod/
    __init__.py      ← Makes canvod a REGULAR package
    readers/         ← Blocks other packages from contributing

If any installed package adds canvod/__init__.py, it claims exclusive ownership of canvod, breaking all other sub-packages.

After uv sync installs all packages:

site-packages/
  canvod/             ← Python merges all contributors here
    readers/          ← from canvod-readers
    auxiliary/        ← from canvod-auxiliary
    grids/            ← from canvod-grids
    vod/              ← from canvod-vod
    store/            ← from canvod-store
    store_metadata/   ← from canvod-store-metadata
    viz/              ← from canvod-viz
    config/           ← from canvod-config
    utils/            ← from canvod-utils
    ops/              ← from canvod-ops
    preflight/        ← from canvod-preflight

items.title: Build configuration
items.text:
The uv_build backend uses a dotted module-name to produce the correct wheel structure:

# packages/canvod-readers/pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires      = ["uv_build>=0.13.0,<0.14.0"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-name = "canvod.readers"   # dot → namespace package

The dot in "canvod.readers" tells uv_build:

  1. Treat canvod/ as a namespace (do not include __init__.py for it).
  2. Package only the readers/ subdirectory and its contents.

items.title: Wheel contents
items.text:
canvod_readers-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
  canvod/
    readers/                 ← package starts here (has __init__.py)
      __init__.py
      base.py
  canvod_readers-0.1.0.dist-info/
    METADATA
    WHEEL
    RECORD

Note

The wheel contains canvod/readers/ but no canvod/__init__.py. This is correct: the absence of __init__.py is what makes it a namespace.

items.title: Import resolution
items.text:
When Python processes from canvod.readers import Rnxv3Obs:

  1. canvod: no __init__.py found \(\rightarrow\) namespace package (open for extension).
  2. readers: has __init__.py \(\rightarrow\) regular package (standard import).
  3. Rnxv3Obs: imported from canvod/readers/__init__.py.

items.title: Independent installation
items.text:
Because each sub-package is self-contained, users install only what they need:

uv add canvod-readers                # readers only
uv add canvod-readers canvod-store   # subset
uv add canvodpy                      # everything

items.title: Verification
items.text:
import canvod

print(canvod.__file__)  # AttributeError: namespace packages have no __file__

from canvod import readers

print(readers.__file__)  # e.g. …/site-packages/canvod/readers/__init__.py

items.title: Common pitfalls
items.text:
Adding __init__.py to the namespace directory

src/canvod/__init__.py converts the namespace into a regular package, preventing all other packages from contributing to canvod.*.

Incorrect module-name

# WRONG: creates a regular top-level package
module-name = "canvod_readers"

# CORRECT: creates a namespace sub-package
module-name = "canvod.readers"

items.title: Design principles
items.text:
This page explains the rules that shape canVODpy and why they exist. Each section says what the rule is, why canVODpy follows it, and where the code enforces it. Architecture describes the packages and how data flows through them.

Some of these rules can look like settings that you could switch off. They aren't: each one protects the data from a mistake that would otherwise go unnoticed.

items.title: One data shape everywhere
items.text:
Every reader returns an xarray.Dataset with two dimensions:

  • epoch: the time of the observation;
  • sid: the signal identifier, SV|Band|Code, for example G01|L1|C.

All later steps work on these two dimensions only: the matching of canopy and reference receivers, the VOD calculation, and the store. They never ask whether the data came from RINEX, SBF, or NMEA. A new reader only has to return the same shape.

canvod.readers.validate_dataset checks the output of every reader:

  • the two dimensions;
  • the signal coordinates sv, system, band, code, freq_center, freq_min, and freq_max;
  • the data variables, every one on (epoch, sid);
  • the attributes Created, Software, Institution, and File Hash.

It lists every problem it finds and then raises a ValueError. VOD datasets have their own check, canvod.readers.validate_vod_dataset: the same dimensions and coordinates, and the variables VOD, theta and phi, with the angles in radians. The VOD store runs it on every VOD write.

A reader can add more variables, such as further observables. It can't leave out what the check requires.

items.title: Problems stop the run before it reads a file
items.text:
Before a run reads a file, it finds the files of every receiver and checks them. The run stops, and lists the files concerned, if:

  • two files map to the same canVOD file name;
  • two files of the same type cover overlapping time spans, for example a daily file next to the 15-minute files of the same day;
  • one folder holds the files of more than one receiver.

There is no option to skip these files and go on. Two files for the same hours would write those epochs twice, and the files of two receivers in one folder would be stored under the wrong receiver. Looking at a list of files costs less than finding wrong data in a store later.

The checks live in canvodpy.orchestrator.discovery. canvodpy run, Site.pipeline(), and the Airflow tasks all use it. canvodpy config validate, and validate_data_dirs() in Airflow, run the same checks without processing anything. They also list the files that a run passes over because neither the naming convention nor a naming recipe recognizes them.

items.title: Every write is a versioned commit
items.text:
Every write to a canVODpy store ends with a commit. The commit is a snapshot of the whole store, with an ID. Later writes add new snapshots and never change old ones. Only store maintenance deletes old snapshots: canvodpy store maintain, or canvodpy store maintain-due after you turn it on in the settings (maintenance.enabled).

A published VOD time series has to be traceable to the data that produced it. If you find a processing error and process the data again, the first and the corrected results stay apart, each under its own snapshot ID. You can cite that ID in a paper or a data publication. A bad write doesn't destroy the good state before it: Icechunk's reset_branch moves a branch back to an earlier snapshot.

canvod-store uses Icechunk for this. Each write opens a session, writes into it and commits it. To see the history:

  • store.get_ops_log() lists the operations on the store;
  • store.plot_commit_graph() draws the commits as a graph, with Icechunk's repo.ancestry_graph();
  • canvodpy store log prints both in the terminal.

To read the store as it was at an earlier commit, open a read-only session on that snapshot: store.repo.readonly_session(snapshot_id=...).

Try it in a notebook

Open Icechunk store in molab, the online notebook service of marimo.

items.title: Packages depend only on the layers below them
items.text:
The packages form layers: foundation, data input, computation, persistence, presentation, and orchestration. A package imports only from packages in its own layer or below. Architecture lists which package sits in which layer.

This lets you use one part on its own. For example, you can run the VOD calculation on data from another source without a store or a reader. It also lets you test each package on its own.

Each package declares its dependencies in its pyproject.toml. canvodpy/tests/test_package_boundaries.py makes sure that no package imports the canvodpy umbrella package. canvod-utils depends on no other canVODpy package.

One exception remains: VODCalculator.from_icechunkstore() in canvod-vod imports canvod-store, which canvod-vod doesn't declare. The method is left over from development and is removed with the next major version. The old names store_grid, load_grid, and AnalysisStorage in canvod-grids also import canvod-store; they moved to canvod-store and are removed with the next major version as well.

items.title: The filename says what the file holds
items.text:
A canVOD file name holds everything that identifies the file: site, receiver, date and start time, the time span the file covers, the sampling interval, and the file format. No database is needed to know what a file holds or which receiver recorded it, and that information survives when the file is copied.

From the name alone, a run:

  • assigns the file to its day and its receiver, in any folder layout;
  • finds duplicates and overlapping files before it reads any of them;
  • picks the reader from the file type: rnx, sbf, nmea, or the type of an installed reader plugin.

Which canopy receiver is paired with which reference receiver is set in the settings, under vod_analyses, not read from the names.

The convention is defined in canvod-preflight (CanVODFilename). Files with other names are read through a naming recipe of the optional canvod-filemap extension (see Optional extensions). The recipe gives each file a canVOD file name and never renames the file itself. All later steps use the canVOD file name; the file's own path is used only to open it. The fields of the name are listed in canvod-preflight.

Try it in a notebook

Open Naming convention in molab, the online notebook service of marimo.

items.title: The same data is never written twice by default
items.text:
Before a file's data goes into the GNSS store, the run checks three things:

  1. Does the store already hold a file with the same hash?
  2. Does the file's time span overlap data already in the store?
  3. Does the file's time span overlap another file of the same batch?

A file with the same hash counts as already stored. What happens then depends on gnss_store_strategy in the settings:

  • skip, the default: the data isn't written, and the run logs the file.
  • overwrite: the epochs of the file's time span are deleted and written again.
  • unsafe_append: the data is written again on top of what's there. The store then holds the same epochs twice. Use it only if you have a specific reason.

A file with another hash whose time span overlaps stored data (check 2) is a conflict between two files, and neither is preferred silently: with skip, the run stops and names both files, the receiver, and the time spans. To replace the stored data with the new file, run those days with overwrite; the log book records the file as overwritten. The check runs again just before each commit, against the files that other runs stored meanwhile. A file that overlaps another file of the same batch (check 3) is skipped and logged.

Epochs stored twice break the matching of canopy and reference receivers without an error. With skip, running the same job twice, for example after a crash, leaves the store as it was after the first run.

The run makes the three checks in _check_existing_with_temporal_overlap() of the orchestrator, and the hash and time span checks again in _check_stored_overlaps() just before each commit.

items.title: Code principles
items.text:
Four rules apply to all canVODpy code. Reviews check new code against them.

Explicit over implicit. A problem stops the code with a message that says what to do. Nothing fails silently, and nothing falls back to a default silently. A default that you can see is fine: one in a function signature, or one documented on a settings model. Library code that reads the settings file behind the caller's back, or picks a value when something goes wrong, isn't. Entry points such as canvodpy run and Site read the settings and pass the values down. One exception is deliberate: a long canvodpy run doesn't stop for one bad file. It warns, names the file, and goes on.

One implementation per task. Every task has one code path, which the command line, the Python API, and Airflow all use. Two implementations of the same task drift apart and give different results. When two exist, the older one is deprecated and its warning names the one that stays.

Composition over inheritance. Objects get the objects they work with passed in, instead of inheriting behavior. Inheritance is used for Pydantic models and to implement an interface.

Interfaces are abstract base classes. Readers, ephemeris providers, VOD calculators, grid builders, and preprocessing steps implement an abstract base class: GNSSDataReader, EphemerisProvider, VODCalculator, BaseGridBuilder, and Op. A class that lacks a method then fails when you create it, not halfway through a run.

Next: architecture · API levels · contributor setup · developing with coding agents

items.title: Development tooling
items.text:
canVODpy uses a modern Python toolchain built almost entirely on the Astral ecosystem.

  • uv

    Replaces pip, venv, pip-tools, and twine in a single binary. Manages Python versions, virtual environments, dependency resolution, and builds.

    astral.sh/uv

  • ruff

    Linter + formatter in one tool. Implements 700+ rules from flake8, pylint, black, and isort at \(10\times\) to \(100\times\) their speed.

    astral.sh/ruff

  • ty

    Type checker replacing mypy. Early development (alpha) but already significantly faster for large codebases.

    docs.astral.sh/ty

  • just

    Task runner with simpler syntax than Make. All common development tasks (test, check, docs, settings) are just <command> away.

    github.com/casey/just

items.title: Core tools
items.text:
uv: package manageruv_build: build backendruff: linter + formatterty: type checker 
uv sync                  # Install all dependencies (workspace-aware)
uv add numpy             # Add a runtime dependency
uv add --dev pytest      # Add a dev dependency
uv run pytest            # Run in the managed environment
uv build                 # Build a wheel
uv publish               # Publish to PyPI

uv sync resolves uv.lock and creates or updates the shared workspace .venv at the repo root; all 12 packages share a single environment.

The scripts under scripts/ that need no canvodpy package (release.py, analyze_dependencies.py, check_agent_docs.py, check_package_imports.py) declare their Python version and dependencies in a # /// script block at the top (inline script metadata, PEP 723). uv run --script scripts/release.py runs such a script in its own small environment, without the workspace; the just recipes call them that way.

Configuration in pyproject.toml:

[project]
dependencies = ["numpy>=2.0", "xarray>=2024.0"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["pytest>=9.0", "ruff>=0.15", "ty>=0.0.44"]

Builds wheel and sdist with native namespace package support:

# packages/canvod-readers/pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires      = ["uv_build>=0.13.0,<0.14.0"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-name = "canvod.readers"   # dot → namespace package

All 12 workspace packages use uv_build as their build backend.

ruff check .          # Lint
ruff check . --fix    # Lint with auto-fix
ruff format .         # Format

Configuration (workspace root pyproject.toml, inherited by all packages):

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py314"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "UP", "B", "RUF"]

Philosophy: catch real bugs, enforce consistent formatting, don't fight scientists over naming or style. Dropped stylistic rules (N, SIM, C4, PIE, PT) that add noise without catching bugs.

Type annotations are optional labels on function inputs/outputs; ty checks that they are consistent, catching a class of bugs before you run the code.

uv run ty check packages/canvod-readers/src/canvod/readers/
uv run ty check canvodpy/src/canvodpy/

Configured at the workspace root pyproject.toml:

[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.14"

Blocking in canVODpy

ty runs in the pre-push hook and in CI (the type_consistency job of code_quality.yml). A type error blocks the push and the pull request. [tool.ty.src] in pyproject.toml lists the files it leaves out. Run just check-types to see the errors.

items.title: Supporting tools
items.text:
just: task runnerpytest: testingpre-commit, Git hooksConventional CommitsZensical + beautiful-mermaid

Recipes are defined in Justfile at the repo root. just --list shows all recipes, sorted into groups such as setup, run and settings, stores, tests and docs.

All common tasks are single commands:

just test             # Run the full test suite
just check            # Lint + format + type-check
just hooks            # Install pre-commit hooks
just docs             # Preview documentation locally
just docs-build       # Build static documentation
just docs-lint        # Check the language of the docs
just docs-links       # Check every link of the built docs
just config-init      # Scaffold canvod-settings.yaml from template
just config-validate  # Validate config files
just --list           # Show all available commands

uv run pytest                        # All tests
uv run pytest --cov=canvod           # With coverage
uv run pytest -m "not integration"   # Skip integration tests
uv run pytest packages/canvod-readers/tests/

Integration tests are marked @pytest.mark.integration. They are not excluded by default; pass -m "not integration" to skip them for a fast unit-only run.

just hooks    # Install hooks (run once after clone)

Configured in .pre-commit-config.yaml. ruff and ty use repo: local so pre-commit uses the same versions as the project:

repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-check
        entry: uv run --locked ruff check --fix
        stages: [pre-commit]
      - id: ruff-format
        entry: uv run --locked ruff format
        stages: [pre-commit]
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv-pre-commit
    hooks:
      - id: uv-lock
        stages: [pre-commit]
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: check-added-large-files
      - id: detect-private-key
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
  - repo: https://github.com/commitizen-tools/commitizen
    hooks:
      - id: commitizen
        stages: [commit-msg]
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: ty-check
        entry: uv run --locked ty check
        stages: [pre-push]

Ruff, uv-lock, and file hygiene hooks run at the pre-commit stage and block the commit on failure. Commitizen validates the message at commit-msg. ty-check runs at the pre-push stage (not on every commit), so type errors surface before reaching the remote but without slowing down local commits. The tools run with uv run --locked: they never rewrite uv.lock, and fail when it is out of date (run uv lock).

Commits must follow the format type: short description where type is one of feat, fix, chore, docs, or refactor. commitizen validates this at the commit-msg git hook stage and blocks non-conforming messages. This powers the automated changelog.

feat: add Fibonacci grid tessellation       ✅
fix(store): handle empty metadata table     ✅
docs(aux): clarify SP3 interpolation        ✅
added new grid                              ❌  (no type prefix)

Monorepo scopes (optional but encouraged): readers, aux, grids, vod, store, viz, utils, naming, orchestrator, diagnostics, ops, ci, docs, deps.

Documentation is built with Zensical, a Rust+Python wrapper around MkDocs Material:

just docs          # Preview locally (wraps uv run zensical serve --open)
just docs-build    # Build static site (wraps uv run zensical build)

Two checks keep the pages correct:

  • just docs-lint checks the language with Vale and its Google style package (.vale.ini). Project words that are spelled correctly go in .vale/styles/config/vocabularies/canvodpy/accept.txt. Pass a path to check a single page: just docs-lint docs/users/index.md.
  • just docs-links builds the site and checks every link with lychee (lychee.toml): links between pages, anchors, and links to other sites. Install lychee once with brew install lychee.

Write diagrams as Mermaid code blocks inside the page; the browser renders them. docs/diagrams/ holds only files that a page embeds.
