items.title: rechunk_group(group_name, chunks, source_branch='main', temp_branch=None, promote_to_main=True, delete_temp_branch=True)
items.text:
Rechunk a group with optimal chunk sizes.

Zarr arrays have a fixed chunk shape once created — writing with mode="r+" onto an existing array cannot change chunk boundaries, it can only update values within the existing grid (verified 2026-07-08: a previous version of this method used mode="r+", which silently failed to change on-disk chunking whenever the request didn't align with the current chunks). Actually changing chunk size requires a destructive mode="w" rewrite of the group, which also wipes the group's nested subgroups (metadata/ table, metadata/sbf_obs) — so this method copies that subtree back afterward via a raw recursive Zarr copy (see _copy_zarr_subtree), all on a temporary branch, before main is ever touched. The copy handles canvod-store's two-level-deep metadata/{table,sbf_obs} nesting.

Both the data read and the subtree copy are pinned to the exact snapshot captured at the start of this call. If source_branch moves before the promotion, the promotion is refused with BranchMovedError (the new commits would be dropped) and the rechunked data stays on temp_branch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default group_name str

Name of the group to rechunk

required chunks dict[str, int]

Chunking specification, e.g. {'epoch': 180, 'sid': -1}. A group stored in day blocks needs an epoch chunk that divides every day into whole chunks.

required source_branch str

Branch to read original data from (default: "main")

'main' temp_branch str | None

Temporary branch name for rechunked data. If None, uses "{group_name}_rechunked".

None promote_to_main bool

If True, move source_branch to the rechunked snapshot after writing (see promote_branch).

True delete_temp_branch bool

If True, delete temporary branch after promotion (only if promote_to_main=True).

True

Returns:

Type Description str

Snapshot ID of the rechunked data

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If temp_branch already exists, or a day-block group gets no positive epoch chunk.

CadenceError

If the epoch chunks would split a day of a day-block group.

BranchMovedError

If source_branch moved during the rechunk.

items.title: Store manager
items.text:
Research site manager that coordinates RINEX and VOD Icechunk stores.

This module provides the GnssResearchSite class that manages both stores for a research site and provides high-level operations across them.

items.title: GnssResearchSite
items.text:
High-level manager for a GNSS research site with dual Icechunk stores.

This class coordinates between RINEX data storage (Level 1) and VOD analysis storage (Level 2), providing a unified interface for site-wide operations.

Architecture: - GNSS Store: Raw/standardized observations per receiver - VOD Store: Analysis products comparing receiver pairs

Features: - Automatic store initialization from config - Receiver management and validation - Analysis workflow coordination - Unified logging and error handling

Name of the research site (must exist in config).

Maintenance on a store on S3 is not supported yet (#357).

Deliberately not a ValueError: nothing records it as a failed file and carries on. items.title: MyIcechunkStore
items.text:
Core Icechunk store manager for GNSS data.

This class encapsulates all operations on a single Icechunk repository, providing a clean interface for GNSS data storage and retrieval with integrated logging and proper resource management.

Features: - Automatic repository creation/connection - Group management with validation - Session management with context managers - Integrated logging with file contexts - Configurable compression and chunking

Note on "metadata"

This class manages two distinct things both historically called "metadata":

  • File registry ({group}/metadata/table): per-file ingest ledger tracking hashes, temporal ranges, filenames, and paths. Managed by append_metadata(), load_metadata(), backup_metadata_table(), etc.

  • Store metadata (canvod.store_metadata package): store-level provenance (identity, creator, environment, compliance). Written to Zarr root attrs by the orchestrator. See canvod-store-metadata.

items.title: chunk_encoding_for(ds)
items.text:
Build {var: {"chunks": (...)}} matching self.chunk_strategy.

Only meaningful at group creation -- Zarr fixes an array's chunk shape the moment it's first written, so this must be passed as encoding= on the mode="w" call, never on an append (which must match whatever shape creation already fixed).

Without this, chunk_strategies config only ever affected read-side chunking (the chunks= hint passed to xr.open_zarr elsewhere in this class) -- nothing applied it at write time, so the physical on-disk chunk shape was left to Zarr's own default, silently disconnected from config. Confirmed by grepping this file and processor.py for any encoding["chunks"] assignment: there wasn't one anywhere (2026-07-18).

A dim with a configured chunk size (e.g. epoch: 17280) gets exactly that size regardless of how much data is in this particular write -- Zarr supports writing less than one full chunk in the first call and filling the rest on later appends, which is the whole point of fixing chunk shape once at creation. A dim configured -1 (or unconfigured) gets one chunk spanning whatever this write's current size is (e.g. sid: -1 -> the full SID universe already present at creation).

Check if a group exists.

Notes

Checks membership directly against the opened root group rather than via :meth:get_group_names/:meth:list_groups -- those only enumerate top-level Zarr group keys (root.group_keys()), so for a nested group_name like a VOD analysis group, membership in that flat list is always False even when the group exists. Confirmed 2026-07-21: this previously caused every VOD write after a group's first to take the mode="w" (full overwrite) branch in :meth:write_or_append_vod_group instead of appending, silently destroying all previously-written VOD data on each subsequent write. Zarr's Group.__contains__ supports slash-separated nested paths directly, so this works for both flat GNSS receiver names (no behavior change there) and nested VOD group names (the actual fix).

items.title: add_group_variables(group_name, variables, step, software, branch='main')
items.text:
Add variables computed from the data already in a group.

For example the grid cells of every observation (canvod.ops.assign_grid_cells_in_store). Only the new variables are written; the group's other variables, its attributes, its log book and its other subgroups stay as they are. The write is staged on a temporary branch and moved to branch with :meth:promote_branch.

The log book receives one group-wide row (:data:GROUP_WIDE_ACTION) whose preprocessing record holds step. From then on, the preprocessing of the data already in the group counts as their own plus step (:meth:preprocessing_records), so a later write is accepted only if it was preprocessed with step as well, and thus carries the new variables too.

forks come from session, which had no changes of its own when they were made; they hold the days the worker pool wrote (:mod:canvodpy.orchestrator.vod_phase). Under the store's commit lock: merge them, rebase onto commits made since the session was opened, write the days not in a fork (VodDayWrite.in_fork), add a log-book row per day and commit.

items.title: write_or_append_vod_groups_batch(items, branch='main', dedup=True)
items.text:
Write/append multiple VOD analysis groups in one fork/merge batch.

The same cross-group parallelization RinexDataProcessor uses for GNSS receiver groups (_write_receiver_batch_forked), applied to VOD analysis groups: any brand-new analysis group is created directly on its own clean session that commits alone (pre-pass) -- verified empirically (see _write_receiver_batch_forked's docstring) that Session.merge() silently drops a fork's data if the base session it merges into had its own pending uncommitted writes before .fork() was called, so new-group creation and forked appends can never safely share one session. Only groups that already exist go through the fork/merge phase; a brand-new group's pre-pass write is its entire contribution to this batch (a VOD write is exactly one dataset per group per call, unlike GNSS's many-files-per-group-per- day case, so there is never leftover data for a newly-created group to append afterward).

Fail-fast: if any group's forked write raises, no merge or commit happens for the fork/merge phase -- a partial merge would silently drop a group's data from an apparently-successful commit. A pre-pass commit that already landed before a later fork failure is safe to leave in place: the next retry's dedup check sees that group's data as already-committed and won't re-attempt it.

items.title: should_skip_file(group_name, file_hash, time_start, time_end, branch='main')
items.text:
Check whether a file should be skipped before processing and writing.

Thin public wrapper around :meth:metadata_row_exists that returns a simple (skip, reason) pair instead of a DataFrame, suitable for use in Airflow task functions as an early-exit optimization.

This method is an early-exit optimization: it avoids opening a write session for files that are already present. Pass dedup=True to :meth:write_or_append_group to make the store the authoritative final gate (runs the same check again before writing).

Checks performed (in order):

  1. Hash match — file was previously ingested (exact duplicate).
  2. Temporal overlap — incoming time range overlaps existing epochs.

Layer 3 (intra-batch overlap) is not applicable here because task functions process files one at a time.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default group_name str

Icechunk group name.

required file_hash str or None

Hash from dataset.attrs["File Hash"]. When None the check is skipped and (False, "") is returned.

required time_start datetime64

First epoch of the incoming dataset.

required time_end datetime64

Last epoch of the incoming dataset.

required branch str

Branch name in the Icechunk repository.

"main"

Returns:

Type Description tuple[bool, str]

(True, "hash_match"): exact duplicate, skip. (True, "temporal_overlap"): overlapping time range, skip. (False, ""): safe to ingest.

Cheap on-disk entry counts for manifests/snapshots/transactions.

A directional proxy for Icechunk-internal growth (manifest count, snapshot count) without walking the full store. Deliberately excludes chunks/ (can reach millions of entries -- not cheap) and only applies to local-filesystem-backed stores; returns {} for anything else (e.g. S3/GCS) since os.scandir doesn't apply.

Reads only the index array's shape (no full table load) -- cheap enough to log alongside every dedup check, so growth in batch_check/check_temporal_overlaps duration can be directly correlated against store size instead of assumed.

items.title: source_file_hashes(group_name, start, end, branch='main')
items.text:
Hashes of the ingested files whose data overlaps [start, end].

Read from group_name's log book, in ingest order and without duplicates. Rows recording a file that was skipped as already ingested (exists is "True" and nothing was written) are ignored, so each file counts once however often it was re-run.

Used as the provenance of a dataset read back from the store for that range, e.g. the daily inputs of a VOD computation.

items.title: load_metadata_for_dedup(group_name, branch='main')
items.text:
{group_name}'s metadata table at the tip of branch.

Read whole the first time, afterwards only the rows committed since (:class:~canvod.store_metadata.log_book.LogBooks): a run asks for it every day, and a whole read grows with the store (ADR 0021).

batch_check_existing/check_temporal_overlaps each used to call load_metadata() independently -- two full-table reads per batch, growing with store size (confirmed against a real backfill: batch_check duration tracked metadata_rows almost exactly, ~5x over 41,597 rows). Callers needing both checks should load once here and pass the result to both via their metadata_df parameter. Returns None (not an empty DataFrame) when the group/metadata doesn't exist yet, so callers can distinguish "nothing to check against" from "failed to load" without re-attempting the load.

items.title: expire_old_snapshots(days=None, branch='main', delete_expired_branches=False, delete_expired_tags=False)
items.text:
Expire snapshots older than the given retention period.

Metadata-only "soft delete": rewrites ancestry so expired snapshots become unreachable from any surviving branch/tag. No objects (manifests, chunks, snapshot files) are deleted at this stage — call garbage_collect() separately to reclaim storage. Keeping this expire-only (previously it also ran GC internally) is what lets a caller run GC exactly once via maintenance() instead of twice per call.

Never invoke this automatically inside the pipeline's write path: it's an administrative operation, not safe to run casually alongside active writes. Use a generous days margin (weeks to months, not hours) so it can never touch anything from an in-flight write session.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default days int | None

Number of days to retain snapshots. Defaults to 90 (weeks-to- months cadence).

None branch str

Branch to apply expiration on.

"main" delete_expired_branches bool

Whether to delete branches pointing to expired snapshots. Matches Icechunk's own safe default: flip only deliberately.

False delete_expired_tags bool

Whether to delete tags pointing to expired snapshots. Do not set True if using keeper tags (create_keeper_tag) — it would delete them along with any other expired-tip tag.

False

Returns:

Type Description set[str]

Expired snapshot IDs.

Raises:

Type Description FileNotFoundError

If the store was opened without settings.

items.title: garbage_collect(days=90, *, dry_run=False)
items.text:
Physically delete objects no longer reachable from any branch/tag.

Only removes what a prior expire_old_snapshots() (or manual ref deletion) already made unreachable — this does not itself expire anything. Always run with dry_run=True first on a store that hasn't been GC'd before, especially one with a large accumulated backlog: there's no documented cost model for GC time/memory at scale, so a first-ever run's duration is unknown until measured.

Not safe to run casually alongside active writes — the cutoff must predate the start of any concurrently-running write session, and only one expire/GC operation should run at a time. Icechunk does have self-protection against races with new commits arriving mid-run (it restarts, bounded retries, rather than deleting something a concurrent writer needs), but that's not a substitute for a generous cutoff margin.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default days int

Objects older than this (by the same write-time semantics as expire_old_snapshots) are eligible for deletion.

90 dry_run bool

Report what would be deleted without deleting anything.

False

Returns:

Type Description dict

Summary of (would-be-)deleted objects.

Raises:

Type Description FileNotFoundError

If the store was opened without settings, also for a dry run, so maintenance behaves one way.

items.title: maintenance_due(expire_interval_days, gc_delay_days, manifest_count_threshold=None)
items.text:
Determine whether scheduled expiration/GC/manifest compaction are due.

Used by canvodpy store maintain-due (a cron-safe, unattended entry point -- see processing.storage.maintenance config). The repo's own ops log (:meth:get_ops_log) is the source of truth for "when did maintenance last actually run": it is written atomically by Icechunk itself as part of the same operation, so it cannot drift the way a separate marker file could (deleted, stale-copied across hosts on a shared mount, or never written if a prior run crashed after the real operation completed but before a marker write). Confirmed empirically (2026-07-20, throwaway store): a real expire_old_snapshots() call always writes an ExpirationRan entry (even when zero snapshots were actually expired -- root/tip snapshots are protected); garbage_collect(dry_run=True) does not write a GCRan entry, only a real (non-dry-run) GC does -- so a dry run correctly never counts as "GC happened" here.

GC is only ever considered due after a qualifying expiration, and never again for the same expiration -- physical deletion should lag the (reversible-in-effect) soft-delete by gc_delay_days, per the skill doc's "expire every 1-2 months, GC every 15-30 days" guidance.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default expire_interval_days int

Re-run expiration if this many days have passed since the most recent ExpirationRan entry (or if there is none yet).

required gc_delay_days int

Run GC this many days after the most recent expiration, once per expiration (skipped if GC already ran since that expiration).

required manifest_count_threshold int | None

Trigger rewrite_manifests() (manifest compaction) when :meth:dir_entry_counts's manifests count reaches this. Unlike expiration/GC, rewrite_manifests() writes no distinguishing ops-log entry -- it logs as an ordinary NewCommit, indistinguishable from a data-ingest commit -- so due-ness is measured directly from current fragmentation rather than time-since-last-ops-log-entry. None (default) always reports manifests_due=False (caller opted out via manifests_enabled=False). Returns False (not an error) if the store isn't local-filesystem-backed (:meth:dir_entry_counts returns {} for S3/GCS).

None

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, Any]

expire_due (bool), gc_due (bool), manifests_due (bool), last_expire (datetime | None), last_gc (datetime | None), manifest_count (int | None).

items.title: compact_manifests(branch='main')
items.text:
Consolidate all of a branch's fragmented manifests in one commit.

Thin wrapper over repo.rewrite_manifests(): canvodpy's write pattern (one to_icechunk() call per file within a batch, e.g. 96 fifteen-minute files/receiver-day) creates one new manifest per flush, not per commit -- a single day's ingest for one receiver can create ~96 manifests. This rewrites them back to the currently-configured splitting boundaries.

Uses commit_method="new_commit" deliberately, not "amend": amend replaces the immediately-preceding commit's own message/ metadata rather than merging with it, and _append_to_icechunk already attaches structured provenance (receiver, date, file hashes) to every ingest commit -- amending could silently clobber that. An explicit, separate, auditable commit matches the precedent expire/GC already set. Like every commit, it records software, environment and settings as commit metadata (:func:canvod.store_metadata.rewrite_manifests).

Like expire_old_snapshots()/garbage_collect(), this is an administrative operation -- never call it while a pipeline run is active against this branch (ordinary commit conflict-retry semantics apply, but a still-draining worker pool committing per-file would just make every retry lose, burning cycles for nothing).

Does not shrink on-disk manifest count by itself -- confirmed empirically (2026-07-20, throwaway store, 300 commits): compaction adds a new, consolidated manifest set but leaves the old fragmented ones on disk (399 -> 401 manifests immediately after compacting); only a subsequent expire_old_snapshots() + garbage_collect() actually reclaims them (399 -> 2 in the same test). This mirrors GC's own relationship to expiration -- don't expect dir_entry_counts()['manifests'] to drop right after calling this; it drops after the next expire/GC cycle instead.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default branch str

Branch to compact.

"main"

Returns:

Type Description str

Snapshot ID of the compaction commit.

items.title: rechunk_group(group_name, chunks, source_branch='main', temp_branch=None, promote_to_main=True, delete_temp_branch=True)
items.text:
Rechunk a group with optimal chunk sizes.

Zarr arrays have a fixed chunk shape once created — writing with mode="r+" onto an existing array cannot change chunk boundaries, it can only update values within the existing grid (verified 2026-07-08: a previous version of this method used mode="r+", which silently failed to change on-disk chunking whenever the request didn't align with the current chunks). Actually changing chunk size requires a destructive mode="w" rewrite of the group, which also wipes the group's nested subgroups (metadata/ table, metadata/sbf_obs) — so this method copies that subtree back afterward via a raw recursive Zarr copy (see _copy_zarr_subtree), all on a temporary branch, before main is ever touched. The copy handles canvod-store's two-level-deep metadata/{table,sbf_obs} nesting.

Both the data read and the subtree copy are pinned to the exact snapshot captured at the start of this call. If source_branch moves before the promotion, the promotion is refused with BranchMovedError (the new commits would be dropped) and the rechunked data stays on temp_branch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default group_name str

Name of the group to rechunk

required chunks dict[str, int]

Chunking specification, e.g. {'epoch': 180, 'sid': -1}. A group stored in day blocks needs an epoch chunk that divides every day into whole chunks.

required source_branch str

Branch to read original data from (default: "main")

'main' temp_branch str | None

Temporary branch name for rechunked data. If None, uses "{group_name}_rechunked".

None promote_to_main bool

If True, move source_branch to the rechunked snapshot after writing (see promote_branch).

True delete_temp_branch bool

If True, delete temporary branch after promotion (only if promote_to_main=True).

True

Returns:

Type Description str

Snapshot ID of the rechunked data

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If temp_branch already exists, or a day-block group gets no positive epoch chunk.

CadenceError

If the epoch chunks would split a day of a day-block group.

BranchMovedError

If source_branch moved during the rechunk.

items.title: create_keeper_tag(receiver, yyyydoy, snapshot_id)
items.text:
Tag a per-(receiver, date) commit as a permanent retention keeper.

Part of the tag-based retention scheme: tagging keep/{receiver}/{yyyydoy} after each commit means a later expire_old_snapshots(delete_expired_tags=False) run can safely prune everything else while these specific snapshots stay time-travelable forever. Additive and inert on its own — creating a tag doesn't expire or delete anything.

Never raises: a tag name collision (already exists, or was previously deleted — Icechunk tag names are never reusable) is logged and skipped rather than failing the pipeline write that called this.

Snapshot to tag — typically the just-committed snapshot.

required

items.title: Analysis storage
items.text:
Persistent storage for precomputed analysis results via Icechunk.

Stores dataset+grid-specific analysis outputs in an Icechunk repository under metadata/{dataset_name}/{grid_name}/:

  • weights – per-cell weight arrays (ncells,).
  • filter_masks – per-observation statistical masks (epoch × sid).
  • spatial_masks – per-cell geometric selection masks (ncells,).
  • statistics – per-cell aggregated statistics (ncells,).

Classes:

Read / write / delete analysis metadata for a single Icechunk store.

metadata/{dataset_name}/{grid_name}/
├── weights/              # (ncells,)
│   ├── observation_count
│   ├── solid_angle
│   └── combined
├── filter_masks/         # (epoch, sid)
│   ├── mask_iqr
│   └── mask_zscore
├── spatial_masks/        # (ncells,)
│   ├── mask_north
│   └── mask_high_elevation
└── statistics/           # (ncells,)
    ├── obs_count
    ├── mean_vod

Utility tools for canVODpy packages.

This module provides common utilities used across all canVODpy packages: - Version management - Date/time utilities for GNSS data - Validation helpers - File hashing - Deprecation warnings

>>> from canvod.utils.tools import get_version_from_pyproject
>>> version = get_version_from_pyproject()

>>> from canvod.utils.tools import YYYYDOY
>>> date = YYYYDOY.from_str("2025024")
>>> print(date.to_datetime())

>>> from canvod.utils.tools import gpsweekday
>>> week, day = gpsweekday("15-01-2025")  # dd-mm-yyyy

>>> from canvod.utils.tools import isfloat
>>> isfloat("3.14")  # True

>>> from canvod.utils.tools import sanitize_directory
>>> sanitize_directory(store_path)  # removes stray .DS_Store files

>>> from canvod.utils.tools import deprecated
>>> @deprecated("Use new_function instead.")
... def old_function(): ...

items.title: YYYYDOY
items.text:
Year and day-of-year (DOY) date representation.

Used throughout canvodpy for GNSS data organization and file naming.

Notes

This is a Pydantic dataclass and uses total_ordering for comparisons.

Attributes:

Name Type Description year int

The year (e.g., 2025).

doy int

Day of year (1-366).

date date

Calculated calendar date.

yydoy str

Short format (YYDDD, e.g., "25001").

Examples:

>>> # From components
>>> d = YYYYDOY(year=2025, doy=1)
>>> d.to_str()
'2025001'

>>> # From date object
>>> import datetime
>>> d = YYYYDOY.from_date(datetime.date(2025, 1, 1))
>>> d.doy
1

>>> # From string
>>> d = YYYYDOY.from_str("2025001")
>>> d.year
2025

>>> # From short string (YYDDD)
>>> d = YYYYDOY.from_yydoy_str("25001")
>>> d.to_str()
'2025001'

Get the installed canvod-utils package version.

Tries importlib.metadata first, which resolves correctly for any install type (wheel, sdist, or editable). Without the importlib.metadata path first, every store write from a non-editable install (a real PyPI release, or a git-sourced install like the demo notebooks use) raised FileNotFoundError here, since callers pass no explicit pyproject_path and expect this to just work.

items.title: Files from a GitHub link
items.text:
Files read from a raw file link in a GitHub repository.

A file is named by its raw file link, at a commit, a tag or a branch::

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<account>/<repo>/<commit>/<path>
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<account>/<repo>/refs/tags/<tag>/<path>
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<account>/<repo>/refs/heads/<branch>/<path>

The user is responsible for what the link points to. Each run fetches the file again; there is no cache. A run fetches a link once, into a folder of the run (:func:run_folder) that only its owner can read; the run's worker processes read the same file, so every part of a run sees the same content. A run folder is removed when the next run of the same process starts (:func:new_run), or when the process ends (the command, the notebook kernel, the Airflow worker). A run is one site; start the next one when the earlier one is done, since its fetched files are gone then.

A file in a private repository needs a GitHub token in the environment variable GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN. canvodpy stores no secrets (ADR "Credentials come from the environment"). The token is only sent to raw.githubusercontent.com, never to the target of a redirect, and never appears in messages or logs.

A link is shown in the terminal (canvodpy doctor, error messages) but never recorded: stores and the run history get only its file name (:func:recorded_name, :func:without_urls). A process that runs more than once starts each run with :func:new_run.

canvod-filemap reads naming recipes with this module; canvodpy reads a settings file given as a URL with it.

items.title: canvod.viz API reference
items.text: 2D and 3D hemispheric visualization tools.

items.title: Package
items.text:
Visualization and plotting utilities for GNSS VOD data.

This package provides 2D and 3D visualization capabilities for hemispherical GNSS grids and VOD data, with both publication-quality (matplotlib) and interactive (plotly) rendering options.

Examples:

2D polar visualization::

from canvod.viz import HemisphereVisualizer2D
from canvod.grids import create_hemigrid

grid = create_hemigrid(grid_type='equal_area', angular_resolution=10.0)
viz = HemisphereVisualizer2D(grid)
fig, ax = viz.plot_grid_patches(data=vod_data, title="VOD Distribution")

Convenience function::

from canvod.viz import visualize_grid, add_tissot_indicatrix

fig, ax = visualize_grid(grid, data=vod_data, cmap='viridis')

Provides consistent API for both publication-quality matplotlib plots and interactive plotly visualizations. Handles styling coordination between different rendering backends.

from canvod.grids import create_hemigrid

items.text:
Add Tissot's indicatrix circles to existing polar plot.

Adds equal-sized circles to visualize grid distortion. In equal-area grids, circles should appear roughly equal-sized. Variation indicates distortion.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ax Axes

Existing polar axis to add circles to

required grid HemiGrid

Grid instance

required radius_deg float

Angular radius of circles in degrees. If None, auto-calculated as angular_resolution / 8.

None n_sample int

Subsample cells (use every nth cell) for performance. If None, shows all cells.

None facecolor str

Fill color for circles

'gold' alpha float

Transparency (0=transparent, 1=opaque)

0.6 edgecolor str

Edge color for circles

'black' linewidth float

Edge line width

0.5 projection ('orthographic', 'equidistant')

Must match the projection used for the underlying ax (see PolarPlotStyle.projection), otherwise circles will be misaligned with the grid patches.

'orthographic'

Returns:

Name Type Description ax Axes

Modified axis with Tissot circles added

items.text:
Stateful orchestrator with factory integration and structured logging. What the command-line tool builds internally.

User-friendly wrapper around GnssResearchSite.

Provides a clean, modern API for site management while using the proven GnssResearchSite implementation internally.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str

Site name from configuration (e.g., "ExampleSite")

required

Attributes:

Name Type Description name str

Site name

receivers dict

All configured receivers

active_receivers dict

Only active receivers

vod_analyses dict

Configured VOD analysis pairs

gnss_store MyIcechunkStore

Access to RINEX data store

vod_store MyIcechunkStore

Access to VOD results store

Examples:

>>> site = Site("ExampleSite")
>>> print(site.receivers)
{'canopy_01': {...}, 'reference_01': {...}}

>>> # Create pipeline
>>> pipeline = site.pipeline()

>>> # Access stores
>>> site.gnss_store.list_groups()

User-friendly wrapper around PipelineOrchestrator.

Provides a clean API for processing workflows while using proven orchestrator logic internally.

All parameters default to None, which means "read from the processing: section of config/canvod-settings.yaml". Explicit values override the config.

Reader format is configured per-receiver via reader_format in the sites: section (default: "auto").

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default site Site or str

Site object or site name

required keep_vars list[str]

RINEX variables to keep. Default: from config.

None aux_agency str

Analysis center for auxiliary data. Default: from config.

None n_workers int

Number of parallel loky worker processes. Default: from config (processing.n_max_threads).

None dry_run bool

If True, simulate without execution.

False max_memory_gb float

Memory budget of the run in GB: the workers and the days per unit are sized to fit it (ADR 0021). Default: from config; without a value there, the memory available when the run starts.

None threads_per_worker int

Threads per loky worker process. Default: from config.

None on_group_written Callable[[str], None]

Called with the receiver-group name each time a group's data for one day finishes writing to Icechunk. Lets a caller drive its own progress display without this class owning any display itself.

None label str

Free-text label of the run, stored in the run history.

None on_discovery_start Callable[[str, Path], None]

Called with the receiver name and its data folder when the run starts finding that receiver's files.

None on_discovery_end Callable[[str, int, int, float], None]

Called with the receiver name, the number of files found, the number of days and the elapsed seconds when the run has found them.

None on_incomplete_day Callable[[str, str, int, int], None]

Called with (receiver, YYYYDOY, files_found, files_expected) for each receiver-day to process that has fewer files than its file length gives for a whole day. Today is not checked.

None on_days_without_vod Callable[[str, list[str]], None]

Called with a receiver and the days in the range on which it has no files while its pair has: those days are not processed and get no VOD.

None A required history required with required

Examples:

>>> # From site object
>>> site = Site("ExampleSite")
>>> pipeline = Pipeline(site)

>>> # Or directly from name
>>> pipeline = Pipeline("ExampleSite")

>>> # Process single date
>>> data = pipeline.process_date("2025001")

>>> # Process range
>>> for date, datasets in pipeline.process_range("2025001", "2025007"):
...     print(f"Processed {date}")

Called with a receiver and the days in the range on which it has no files while its pair has: those days are not processed and get no VOD.

None

Returns:

Type Description Pipeline

Configured pipeline for this site

Examples:

>>> site = Site("ExampleSite")
>>> pipeline = site.pipeline(n_workers=8)
>>> data = pipeline.process_date("2025001")

items.title: failed_receiver_days property
items.text:
Receiver-days of this run that failed.

(receiver, YYYYDOY) pairs, empty while every receiver-day is written or skipped. canvodpy run exits with code 3 when a run has any; the log says why each one failed.

items.text:
End the run and release orchestrator resources.

loky's reusable executor is shared and left running.

items.title: process_date(date)

Process RINEX data for one date.

Name Type Description Default date str

Date in YYYYDOY format (e.g., "2025001" for Jan 1, 2025)

required

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, Dataset]

Processed datasets for each receiver

Examples:

>>> pipeline = Pipeline("ExampleSite")
>>> data = pipeline.process_date("2025001")
>>> print(data.keys())
dict_keys(['canopy_01', 'canopy_02', 'reference_01'])

>>> # Access individual receiver
>>> canopy_data = data['canopy_01']
>>> print(canopy_data.dims)
Dimensions: (epoch: 2880, sv: 32, ...)

items.text:
Process RINEX data for a date range.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default start str

Start date (YYYYDOY)

required end str

End date (YYYYDOY)

required

Yields:

(date_key, datasets) for each processed date

>>> pipeline = Pipeline("ExampleSite")
>>> for date, datasets in pipeline.process_range("2025001", "2025007"):

items.title: run(start=None, end=None, *, update_to_latest=False, vod_analyses=None, calculator='tau_omega')
items.text:
Store the days from start to end, then compute their VOD.

The run of canvodpy run (ADR 0021). The GNSS phase stores the days in units of days and reads nothing back; after each unit, the VOD phase computes the VOD of its days in the same worker pool, from the GNSS store, and commits once (VodComputer.compute_days). Meanwhile, the GNSS phase works on the next unit. A day that failed gets no VOD and stays open for the next run.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default start str

First and last day (YYYYDOY). start is needed unless update_to_latest; without end the run goes to the last day with files.

None end str

First and last day (YYYYDOY). start is needed unless update_to_latest; without end the run goes to the last day with files.

None update_to_latest bool

Process the days from the last stored day on instead of start/end (:meth:update_range); with nothing new, the run yields nothing.

False vod_analyses sequence of str

The VOD analyses to compute; all the site's by default. An empty sequence computes no VOD.

None calculator str

The registered VOD calculator.

"tau_omega"

Yields:

Type Description RunUnit

Per unit, once its VOD is committed: the days stored and what the VOD phase did. A failing VOD phase is logged and reported in RunUnit.vod_error; the run goes on.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If neither start nor update_to_latest is given, or update_to_latest comes with start or end.

NothingStoredError

With update_to_latest, if nothing is stored for the site yet.

Examples:

>>> with Site("ExampleSite").pipeline() as pipeline:
...     for unit in pipeline.run("2025001", "2025007"):
...         print(sorted(unit.days), unit.vod.written)

items.text:
Preview processing plan without execution.

Name Type Description Default start str

YYYYDOY string to start from (inclusive). None previews every available date.

None end str

YYYYDOY string to end at (inclusive). None previews every available date.

None update_to_latest bool

Preview the days a run with update_to_latest processes (:meth:update_range); with nothing new, the plan has no dates.

False

Summary of dates, receivers, and files

Raises:

If update_to_latest comes with start or end.

With update_to_latest, if nothing is stored for the site yet.

Examples:

>>> pipeline = Pipeline("ExampleSite")
>>> plan = pipeline.preview(start="2025001", end="2025003")
>>> print(f"Total files: {plan['total_files']}")

items.title: update_range()
items.text:
The days a run with update_to_latest processes.

It starts on the earliest last stored day in the site's GNSS store, counting only the receivers with new files: after their own last stored day, or on it but not in the store's log book. A day stored while its files were still arriving thus gets the rest, and a retired receiver doesn't hold the start back. It ends on the latest day with files.

Returns:

Type Description tuple[str, str] | None

The first and last day (YYYYDOY); None if no receiver has new files.

Raises:

Type Description NothingStoredError

If nothing is stored for the site yet.

Examples:

>>> with Site("ExampleSite").pipeline(dry_run=True) as pipeline:
...     pipeline.update_range()
('2026293', '2026298')

items.title: Factories
items.text:
Bases: ComponentFactory

Factory for GNSS data readers.

All registered readers must inherit from GNSSDataReader ABC.

Supports two creation modes:

  • By name: ReaderFactory.create("rinex3", fpath=path)
  • By file: ReaderFactory.create_from_file(path) — detects RINEX v2, RINEX v3 and NMEA from the file's content (not SBF).

Examples:

>>> from canvodpy import ReaderFactory
>>> reader = ReaderFactory.create("rinex3", fpath="station.25o")

>>> reader = ReaderFactory.create_from_file("station.25o")

Bases: ComponentFactory

Factory for grid builders.

All registered builders must inherit from BaseGridBuilder ABC.

Examples:

>>> from canvod.grids import EqualAreaBuilder
>>> GridFactory.register("equal_area", EqualAreaBuilder)
>>> grid = GridFactory.create(
...     "equal_area",
...     angular_resolution=5.0,
...     cutoff_theta=75.0,
... )

Bases: ComponentFactory

Factory for VOD calculators.

All registered calculators must inherit from VODCalculator ABC.

Examples:

>>> from canvod.vod import TauOmegaZerothOrder
>>> VODFactory.register("tau_omega", TauOmegaZerothOrder)
>>> calc = VODFactory.create(
...     "tau_omega",
...     canopy_ds=canopy,
...     sky_ds=sky,
... )
>>> vod = calc.calculate_vod()

items.title: create_from_file(fpath, **kwargs) classmethod
items.text:
Auto-detect the file format and create the appropriate reader.

Detects NMEA (a .nmea extension or a first line starting with $), and otherwise RINEX v2 or v3 from the version in the first header line; a RINEX v3 file with signal-strength observables only gets the stripped RINEX v3 reader. SBF files are not detected: create their reader by name.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fpath str or Path

Path to the GNSS data file.

required **kwargs Any

Additional parameters forwarded to the reader constructor.

{}

Returns:

Type Description GNSSDataReader

Instantiated reader for the detected format.

Raises:

Type Description FileNotFoundError

If fpath does not exist.

ValueError

If the format cannot be determined or no reader is registered for the detected format.

items.title: detect_reader(fpath) classmethod
items.text:
Name of the registered reader for the file at fpath.

Decided as in :meth:create_from_file: NMEA by its .nmea extension or its sentences, RINEX by the version in the first header line.

Raises:

Type Description FileNotFoundError

If fpath does not exist.

ValueError

If the format cannot be determined or no reader is registered for the detected format.

items.title: Command line
items.text:
The canvodpy command runs canVODpy from the command line. This page lists every command and option, and canvodpy COMMAND --help prints the same text in the terminal. For a walk through a first run, see Retrieve VOD.

Process GNSS observations into VOD and inspect the stores.

Usage:

$ canvodpy [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

  • --version: Show canvodpy's version and exit.
  • --install-completion: Install completion for the current shell.
  • --show-completion: Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation.
  • --help-all: Show every command with its options, and exit. One command with descriptions: canvodpy COMMAND --help; all of them: https://canvodpy.eu/api/cli/
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

Commands:

  • run: Process GNSS observations into Icechunk...
  • vod: Compute VOD for a range of days from the...
  • vod-reconcile: List the dates that have observations but...
  • doctor: Report canvodpy's version, its...
  • dashboard: Launch the marimo performance dashboard...
  • config: Create, check, show, and edit...
  • store: Inspect the Icechunk stores of the sites...
  • stac: Write the STAC catalog of every store...

items.title: canvodpy run
items.text:
Process GNSS observations into Icechunk stores and compute VOD.

Exits with 0 when every receiver-day is written or skipped, 3 when the run finished but a receiver-day failed (the log says why), and 1 when the run stopped.

Usage:

$ canvodpy run [OPTIONS]

Options:

  • --site <str>: Site name, as defined under sites: in canvod-settings.yaml, for example ExampleSite. One site per run: for several sites, run canvodpy once per site, for example in a shell loop. [required]
  • --start <str>: Start date in YYYYDOY format, for example 2025001. Needed unless --update-to-latest is given.
  • --end <str>: End date in YYYYDOY format, for example 2025007. If omitted, processes up to today.
  • --update-to-latest: Process the days from the last stored day up to the latest day with files, instead of --start and --end. Starts on the earliest last stored day among the receivers with new files (after that day, or on it but not stored yet), so a retired receiver doesn't hold it back.
  • --no-vod / --vod: Skip the VOD calculation: only write the observations to the GNSS store. [default: vod]
  • --label <str>: Free-text label of the run, stored in the run history, for example to group the repetitions of a benchmark.
  • --dry-run / --no-dry-run: Preview processing plan without executing. [default: no-dry-run]
  • --workers <int>: Number of worker processes. Default: from the resource settings in canvod-settings.yaml.
  • -c, --config-dir <path|url>: Configuration directory, holding canvod-settings.yaml and recipes/, or the URL of a settings file in a GitHub repository, fetched by each run (https://raw.githubusercontent.com////.../canvod-settings.yaml). Default: $CANVOD_CONFIG_DIR, else config/ of the canvodpy checkout, else ~/.config/canvodpy.
  • --config <str>: Settings file whose values replace those of canvod-settings.yaml.
  • --ephemeris-source <final|broadcast>: Where the satellite orbits and clocks come from: final uses the SP3 and CLK products of an analysis center, broadcast uses the SatVisibility blocks of the SBF files. Default: from canvod-settings.yaml.
  • --vod-calculator <tau_omega>: VOD calculator to use. [default: tau_omega]
  • --write-catalog: After the run, write the latest STAC catalog of every store under the data root, as canvodpy stac write does.
  • --dashboard: Start the marimo performance dashboard next to this run, in a process of its own. Its startup messages go to a log file, not to this terminal.
  • --dashboard-host <str>: Host for --dashboard to bind to. [default: 127.0.0.1]
  • --dashboard-port <int>: Port for --dashboard to bind to. Default: a free port that the operating system picks.
  • --dashboard-stop-at-end: Stop the dashboard of --dashboard when the run ends. Default: it stays up to show the finished run until you shut it down with its button.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.title: canvodpy vod
items.text:
Compute VOD for a range of days from the GNSS store of a site, one day per worker. Days stored from the same GNSS files are skipped; days without data are listed.

Usage:

$ canvodpy vod [OPTIONS]

Options:

  • --site <str>: Site name, as defined under sites: in canvod-settings.yaml [required]
  • --analysis <str>: VOD analysis name, as defined in site.vod_analyses [required]
  • --start <str>: First day in YYYYDOY format, for example 2025001. Default: the first day of the GNSS store.
  • --end <str>: Last day in YYYYDOY format, for example 2025007. Default: the last day of the GNSS store.
  • --calculator <tau_omega>: VOD calculator to use. [default: tau_omega]
  • -c, --config-dir <path|url>: Configuration directory, holding canvod-settings.yaml and recipes/, or the URL of a settings file in a GitHub repository, fetched by each run (https://raw.githubusercontent.com////.../canvod-settings.yaml). Default: $CANVOD_CONFIG_DIR, else config/ of the canvodpy checkout, else ~/.config/canvodpy.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.text:

  • -c, --config-dir <path|url>: Configuration directory, holding canvod-settings.yaml and recipes/, or the URL of a settings file in a GitHub repository, fetched by each run (https://raw.githubusercontent.com////.../canvod-settings.yaml). Default: $CANVOD_CONFIG_DIR, else config/ of the canvodpy checkout, else ~/.config/canvodpy.

items.text:
Create, check, show, and edit canvod-settings.yaml.

Usage:

$ canvodpy config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

  • --config <path>: Settings file whose values replace those of canvod-settings.yaml.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

Commands:

  • init: Create canvod-settings.yaml from its...
  • validate: Validate the configuration and the...
  • show: Show the settings that canvodpy uses.
  • edit: Open canvod-settings.yaml in $EDITOR.
  • explain: Print what a setting of...

items.title: canvodpy config init
items.text:
Create canvod-settings.yaml from its template, or from a store.

The file goes into the configuration directory that --config-dir sets. Create a naming recipe for each receiver with just naming-init SITE NAME.

With --from-store STORE, the file is written from the store's content settings (a folder or an s3:// URL): the settings that shape its data stay as they are, and the machine values are asked (or left as TODO with --no-interactive).

Usage:

$ canvodpy config init [OPTIONS]

Options:

  • -c, --config-dir <path>: Configuration directory, holding canvod-settings.yaml and recipes/. Default: $CANVOD_CONFIG_DIR, else config/ of the canvodpy checkout, else ~/.config/canvodpy.
  • -f, --force: Overwrite existing files (no effect with --from-store)
  • -i, --interactive: Walk through setup with a guided Q&A instead of hand-editing YAML
  • --from-store <str>: Write the settings of a store from its content settings: a local dir or an s3://bucket/prefix URL
  • --no-interactive: With --from-store: keep the machine-value placeholders (TODO) instead of asking
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.title: canvodpy config validate
items.text:
Validate the configuration and the receiver data it points to.

It finds the data files the same way as canvodpy run, so every error it reports would stop a run or make its results wrong. A settings file written from a store (:meth:init) that still has placeholder values is listed, and the command exits with code 1.

Usage:

$ canvodpy config validate [OPTIONS]

Options:

  • -c, --config-dir <path|url>: Configuration directory, holding canvod-settings.yaml and recipes/, or the URL of a settings file in a GitHub repository, fetched by each run (https://raw.githubusercontent.com////.../canvod-settings.yaml). Default: $CANVOD_CONFIG_DIR, else config/ of the canvodpy checkout, else ~/.config/canvodpy.
  • --config <path>: Settings file whose values replace those of canvod-settings.yaml.
  • --site <str>: Check the data of this site only. Repeat for several sites. Default: all sites.
  • --check-sampling / --no-check-sampling: Read the first file of the first and the last day of each receiver and compare the sampling interval of its data with the one in its canonical name. [default: check-sampling]
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.title: canvodpy config show
items.text:
Show the settings that canvodpy uses.

Usage:

$ canvodpy config show [OPTIONS]

Options:

  • -c, --config-dir <path|url>: Configuration directory, holding canvod-settings.yaml and recipes/, or the URL of a settings file in a GitHub repository, fetched by each run (https://raw.githubusercontent.com////.../canvod-settings.yaml). Default: $CANVOD_CONFIG_DIR, else config/ of the canvodpy checkout, else ~/.config/canvodpy.
  • -s, --section processing|sites|sids: Show this section only. Default: all sections.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

$ canvodpy config edit [OPTIONS]

items.title: canvodpy config explain
items.text:
Print what a setting of canvod-settings.yaml means.

Prints the setting's description, type, limits and default, and a link to its entry in the settings reference. Name a site, receiver or VOD analysis as in your file: sites.my_site.receivers.reference_01.directory.

Usage:

$ canvodpy config explain [OPTIONS] {setting}

Arguments:

  • setting: The setting's path in canvod-settings.yaml, or the end of it (for example gnss_store.epoch). [required]

Options:

  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.title: canvodpy store
items.text:
Inspect the Icechunk stores of the sites and maintain them.

Usage:

$ canvodpy store [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

  • --help: Show this message and exit.

Commands:

  • list: List every configured site's GNSS and VOD...
  • info: Show branches, groups, and stats for one...
  • log: Show the commit history as a graph, or the...
  • maintain: Expire old snapshots of one site's store...
  • maintain-due: Run only the store maintenance that's due,...
  • migrate-metadata: Move a store written before repository...
  • migrate-layout: Move a store written by appending files to...
  • amend: Change the description of a site's store,...
  • migrate: Move a site's stores from canVODpy 0.x to...

Default: $CANVOD_CONFIG_DIR, else config/ of the canvodpy checkout, else ~/.config/canvodpy.
