See canvod-filemap's overview for the recipe format and mapping API, canvod-airflow's overview for DAG structure, deployment, and configuration (canvod-airflow depends on canvodpy, not the other way around), and canvod-adapters' overview for the gnssvod conversion, including how merged VOD bands are imported.

items.title: What happens if an extension isn't installed
items.text: canvodpy imports canvod-filemap only for a receiver whose settings set recipe:. Without a recipe, discovery takes files with canonical canVOD names only, whether or not the package is installed. A receiver with a recipe but without canvod-filemap installed stops the run with an error that says how to install it; it never falls back to guessing file names. See Configuration \(\rightarrow\) Optional: non-canonical filenames.

items.title: Parallel processing
items.text: A run reads many files: one or more per receiver and day. canVODpy reads and writes them in parallel worker processes and commits them to the store in units of days, once per unit. This page explains how a run divides the work and which settings limit its use of the machine.

items.title: How a run divides the work
items.text:
A run works through the days in units of several days. The run sizes the units itself (see Memory use): as many days as the memory budget holds, at most 31; a run of one new day is a unit of one day. Each unit goes through three steps, and the units overlap: while the workers read one unit, the next unit is prepared, and while its days go to VOD, the workers read the next unit.

 days of one unit
        │
        ▼   one thread per day
 1. Prepare: orbit and clock data, receiver positions
        │
        ▼   one task per group of files, in date order
 2. Read and write: worker processes read the files and
        │   write them into forks of the unit
        ▼   when all tasks of the unit are done
 3. Commit: the forks of the unit go into the GNSS store, one commit
        │
        ▼
 the days go to VOD (canvodpy run) or to your loop (Python)
  1. Prepare. Each day of the unit gets its orbit and clock data, downloaded and interpolated or taken from the cache, and the receiver positions. Up to four days of a unit are prepared at the same time, one thread per day, so that the download server gets at most four requests at once. A day whose orbit and clock files are not out yet is left out of the unit and stays open for the next run; the other days go on.
  2. Read and write. A task for the worker processes holds the files of one receiver that share an epoch chunk of the store. With preprocessing set, the chunks are those of the aggregated epochs: a time bin is one of their slots, so files whose epochs fall into one bin are in one task. The worker reads the files, applies the preprocessing (if set), checks for data already in the store, and writes the files into their places in the day's day blocks, in its own fork of the store. No two tasks write the same chunk. The tasks go out in date order and alternate between the receivers, so all receivers of a day finish at about the same time. At most twice as many tasks as workers wait at a time.
  3. Commit. When all tasks of the unit are done, a thread of the main process merges their forks and commits the unit, once per store. It also writes the few files whose epochs reach beyond their task's chunks. A file that fails gets no entry in the store's log book, so the next run tries it again; the other files and days are committed. The commit itself is one for the whole unit: if it fails (a store error, or other runs keep committing first through all tries), every day of the unit is reported as failed and the next run writes them. If another run committed to the store first, the unit is read and written again on top of it. The first day of a new store is a unit of its own, and the first day of a receiver new to the store is read by the workers and written by the main process, since that day creates the store's arrays; the Storage page describes the checks for duplicate data.

When the unit is committed, canvodpy run (and pipeline.run() in Python) computes the VOD of its days: one task per receiver pair and day in the same worker processes, each reading its day from the GNSS store, and one commit of the VOD store for the unit. Nothing is read back for VOD while the observations are written. A day that failed gets no VOD and stays open for the next run; if the VOD of a unit fails, the run says which days are left without VOD and goes on (canvodpy vod-reconcile computes them later). In Python, process_range instead reads each day back and hands it to your loop.

Meanwhile the run goes on with the next unit, which was prepared while this one was read, so the workers don't wait for the preparing. The preparing of the next unit starts once this unit's day blocks are added to the store (a small commit before the tasks go out): next to the preparing, that commit took many times as long. The run goes one unit ahead at most: it waits when a whole unit waits for its VOD or for your loop. So the data of two units can be in memory at the same time.

If your loop stops with an error, the run stops too: the unit being committed is committed, the files still being read are dropped, and the error is raised. Days already written stay in the store; the next run writes the rest. A day whose preparing fails, other than a missing orbit or clock file, is reported as failed for each receiver.

items.title: The worker processes
items.text:
The workers are a reusable process pool of loky, a dependency of canVODpy. They start with the first unit and stay for the next units, so Python and the scientific libraries are loaded once per worker, not once per day.

Before the first file is read, the run prepares the first unit. On a first run this includes downloading the orbit and clock files, so the first minutes of a run can look idle.

The workers are shared by all pipelines in one Python session, and Pipeline.close() leaves them running. They stop after 15 minutes without work, or when Python exits.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The settings are under processing.params in canvod-settings.yaml. resource_mode decides which of them a run uses.

AutomaticManual, for shared servers 
processing:
  params:
    resource_mode: auto

The run starts one worker per physical CPU core, but leaves at least two of the CPU threads free for the operating system, and starts at least one worker; fewer if they do not fit in the memory budget. A second thread per core (hyper-threading, SMT) would add a worker process and its memory, not speed. With auto_uncapped: true the run uses all CPU threads; use that only on a machine nobody else uses.

processing:
  params:
    resource_mode: manual
    n_max_threads: 4            # number of worker processes
    cpu_affinity: [0, 1, 2, 3]  # CPU cores the workers run on
    nice_priority: 10           # lower priority than other programs
Setting Default Meaning resource_mode auto auto chooses the number of workers; manual uses the settings below. n_max_threads none Most worker processes, 1 to 100; fewer run if they do not fit in the memory budget. Required with manual; auto ignores it and warns. auto_uncapped false With auto: one worker per CPU thread, instead of one per physical core with two threads left free. threads_per_worker none (1) Threads that numerical libraries such as OpenBLAS and MKL use in each worker, 1 to 8. If you set OMP_NUM_THREADS or a similar variable yourself, your value applies. cpu_affinity none With manual: the CPU cores the workers run on. Works on Linux and Windows; macOS ignores it. nice_priority -5 With manual: the nice value added to the workers' priority, from -20 (highest) to 19 (lowest). Only an administrator can set a negative value; for other users the workers keep the normal priority. With auto, the run always tries -5.

On a server you share with others, use manual with at most half of the CPU cores and a positive nice_priority, such as 10, so the run gives way to other programs.

items.title: From the command line and from Python
items.text: canvodpy run --workers overrides the settings for one run. In Python, site.pipeline() takes n_workers, max_memory_gb and threads_per_worker. Setting the number of workers this way replaces the choice of resource_mode: auto. The workers' CPU cores and priority always come from the settings file.

items.title: Memory use
items.text:
A run fits its memory budget: max_memory_gb under processing.params, or, without it, the memory available when the run starts. The budget holds two things:

  • The main process: what it holds at the start, plus the data of the days in flight. Since the run goes one unit ahead, that is two units of days.
  • The workers: each holds Python and its libraries, about 0.3 GB, plus its largest task. A task reads the files of one receiver that share an epoch chunk, one after the other, and holds their data until it writes them. A reference receiver paired with several canopy receivers counts once for each pairing.

Before it reads a file, the run estimates both from the size of the files. The workers come first:

workers = min(worker cap, (budget - main process with one day) / largest task)

The worker cap is n_max_threads with manual (or --workers), and the CPU cores minus two with auto. A unit then gets as many days as the rest of the budget holds, at most 31 and at most the days the run has. Larger units spread the main process's work per unit (the growth of the day blocks, the commit) over more days; the limit of 31 keeps what a crash or a lost conflict costs small. If one worker does not fit even with one day, the run stops before it reads a file and says how much memory it needs.

processing:
  params:
    max_memory_gb: 8   # this run uses at most about 8 GB
Setting Default Meaning max_memory_gb none Memory budget of a run in GB. Without it, the memory available when the run starts. With auto and manual alike. In Python, site.pipeline(max_memory_gb=...).

The estimates come from factors measured on the test data, with a margin: reading a file needs about 45 times its size for RINEX v3, 100 times for RINEX v2, 25 times for SBF and 15 times for NMEA, and a task holds about 1.6 times the size of its files once read. For each day in flight, the main process holds about the size of the day's files for RINEX v3, 2.5 times for RINEX v2 and NMEA (small files) and a quarter for SBF, whose files hold much that a run doesn't keep. These were measured keeping only SNR; keeping more observables (keep_gnss_observables) makes the data in memory larger, so set max_memory_gb with that margin. The run writes its sizes to the log (memory_budget): the workers, the days per unit (unit_days) and what set them (unit_limit: memory, max_unit_days, days_to_run, or the deprecated days_per_batch), the tasks per day and per worker, as a warning when the budget lowered the workers or the days per unit. After each task, the worker writes its memory before the task and its peak during the task (worker_memory_peak), so you can check the estimates on your data and set the budget. The VOD phase's tasks log the same event, with task set to compute_vod_into_fork and input_mb 0, since they read from the GNSS store, not from files.

The run also writes the memory use of the machine to the log before each unit (memory_stats). Every run also writes memory, CPU, and disk use every 30 seconds (resource_sample) to the log; the run history keeps the same samples. Diagnostics describes both.

Next in the trail: diagnostics · configuration · architecture

items.title: Your own readers and VOD calculators
items.text:
canvodpy run can read a file format and compute VOD with a model that canvodpy does not ship. Both come from a small Python package of your own, a plugin. Once the plugin is installed in the same environment as canvodpy, its reader is a reader_format in the settings and its VOD calculator a choice of --vod-calculator. You change nothing in canvodpy.

This page shows a complete plugin package. Copy it and replace the parts marked as yours.

Try it in a notebook

Open Your Own VOD Calculator in molab, the online notebook service of marimo.
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: Base classes and factories
items.text:
Each kind of component has an abstract base class, which lists the methods an implementation must have, and a factory, which maps names to the implementing classes. canvodpy registers its built-in classes when it is imported, and the plugins after them.

Factory Base class Built-in names Used by ReaderFactory canvod.readers.base.GNSSDataReader rinex3, rinex3_stripped, rinex2, sbf, nmea reader_format of a receiver VODFactory canvod.vod.calculator.VODCalculator tau_omega canvodpy run --vod-calculator GridFactory canvod.grids.core.grid_builder.BaseGridBuilder equal_area, equal_angle, equirectangular, htm, geodesic, healpix, fibonacci your own scripts only

All three are importable from canvodpy and share these methods:

  • register(name, cls) adds a class. It raises a TypeError if the class doesn't inherit the factory's base class, and a ValueError if the name is already registered. To replace a registered class, pass replace=True.
  • create(name, **kwargs) creates an instance. It raises a ValueError that lists the registered names if name isn't one of them.
  • list_available() returns the registered names.

Because each class inherits an abstract base class, Python refuses to create an instance of a class that lacks one of the required methods: the error comes when the object is created, not halfway through a run.

Plugins can add readers and VOD calculators. A grid builder can only be registered in your own scripts; canvodpy run creates its grids from the settings.
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: How canvodpy finds a plugin
items.text:
A plugin declares entry points in its pyproject.toml: a name and the class it stands for. canvodpy reads two entry point groups:

Group Class inherits The name is used as canvodpy.readers canvod.readers.base.GNSSDataReader reader_format of a receiver canvodpy.vod_calculators canvod.vod.calculator.VODCalculator canvodpy run --vod-calculator <name>

When canvodpy is imported, it imports every installed plugin and checks it. A plugin that cannot be used stops canvodpy with an error that names the plugin's package (see Checks). Fix the plugin or uninstall it.
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: The package
items.text:
my-canvod-plugin/
├── pyproject.toml
└── src/
    └── my_canvod_plugin/
        ├── __init__.py
        ├── reader.py
        └── calculator.py

# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "my-canvod-plugin"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = ["canvodpy"]

[project.entry-points."canvodpy.readers"]
my_format = "my_canvod_plugin.reader:MyFormatReader"

[project.entry-points."canvodpy.vod_calculators"]
my_model = "my_canvod_plugin.calculator:MyModel"

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

A plugin can declare a reader, a calculator, or both. Each name must be new: auto, the built-in reader formats (rinex3, rinex3_stripped, rinex2, sbf, nmea) and the built-in calculator tau_omega are taken.
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: The reader
items.text:
# src/my_canvod_plugin/reader.py
from collections.abc import Iterator
from datetime import datetime
from typing import ClassVar

import xarray as xr
from canvod.readers.base import GNSSDataReader
from canvod.readers.builder import DatasetBuilder
from canvod.utils.tools import file_hash


class MyFormatReader(GNSSDataReader):
    """Reader for the files of my receiver."""

    #: The TYPE field of the files' canVOD names: ...AA.myf
    file_type: ClassVar[str] = "myf"

    @property
    def source_format(self) -> str:
        return "my_format"

    @property
    def file_hash(self) -> str:
        return file_hash(self.fpath)

    def iter_epochs(self) -> Iterator:
        # yours: parse the file, yield one epoch at a time
        ...

    def to_ds(self, keep_data_vars=None, **kwargs) -> xr.Dataset:
        builder = DatasetBuilder(self, time_system="GPS")
        for epoch in self.iter_epochs():
            ei = builder.add_epoch(epoch.timestamp)
            for obs in epoch.observations:
                sig = builder.add_signal(sv=obs.sv, band=obs.band, code=obs.code)
                builder.set_value(ei, sig, "SNR", obs.snr)
        return builder.build(keep_data_vars=keep_data_vars)

    @property
    def start_time(self) -> datetime: ...  # yours: first epoch

    @property
    def end_time(self) -> datetime: ...  # yours: last epoch

    @property
    def systems(self) -> list[str]: ...  # yours: e.g. ["G", "E"]

    @property
    def num_satellites(self) -> int: ...  # yours

What the reader must do:

  • file_type: the file type of its files, 2 to 8 lowercase letters and digits. It is the TYPE field of their canVOD names, so a run finds ROSA01TUW_R_20250010000_15M_05S_AA.myf. Files with other names need a naming recipe (see Configuration).
  • GPS time: the stores hold GPS time only. DatasetBuilder records the time scale you give it; convert other time scales while reading.
  • GLONASS channels: a run passes processing.params.aggregate_glonass_fdma to every reader. A reader that gives GLONASS FDMA signals as aggregated G1/G2 bands only needs nothing more: it refuses false. A reader that can give them per frequency channel sets per_channel_glonass: ClassVar[bool] = True and passes self.aggregate_glonass_fdma on to DatasetBuilder.
  • Every abstract member of GNSSDataReader; Python refuses to create a reader that lacks one. Building a Reader explains each of them, the dataset the reader must return and how to test it.

The satellite angles come from the orbit files, as for RINEX.
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: The VOD calculator
items.text:
# src/my_canvod_plugin/calculator.py
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
from canvod.vod.calculator import VODCalculator


class MyModel(VODCalculator):
    """VOD from the canopy and reference signal strengths, my way."""

    def calculate_vod(self) -> xr.Dataset:
        delta_snr = self.canopy_ds["SNR"] - self.sky_ds["SNR"]
        vod = ...  # yours: from delta_snr and self.canopy_ds["theta"]
        cell_ids = {
            name: self.canopy_ds[name]
            for name in self.canopy_ds.data_vars
            if str(name).startswith("cell_id_")
        }
        return xr.Dataset(
            {
                "VOD": vod,
                "phi": self.canopy_ds["phi"],
                "theta": self.canopy_ds["theta"],
                **cell_ids,
            },
            coords=self.canopy_ds.coords,
        )

canopy_ds holds the data of the canopy receiver and sky_ds the data of the reference receiver. Both are restricted to the epochs and signals they share. Return VOD, phi and theta, and keep the cell_id_* variables that a grid assignment (processing.preprocessing) added.
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: Install and run
items.text:
Install the plugin into the environment canvodpy runs in:

uv add --editable ./my-canvod-plugin

Name the reader in the receivers that record that format (canopy and reference must use the same reader):

# canvod-settings.yaml
sites:
  ExampleSite:
    receivers:
      canopy_01:
        type: canopy
        directory: 02_canopy
        reader_format: my_format
      reference_01:
        type: reference
        directory: 01_reference
        reader_format: my_format

and run with the calculator:

canvodpy run --site ExampleSite --start 2025001 --end 2025007 --vod-calculator my_model

reader_format: auto never chooses a plugin; name it.

The VOD store records the calculator's name in its group names (my_model/<analysis>).
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: Checks
items.text:
When canvodpy is imported, each plugin is checked. Any of these stops canvodpy with an error that names the plugin's package:

  • the class cannot be imported, or the entry point does not name a class;
  • the reader does not inherit GNSSDataReader, the calculator not VODCalculator;
  • the name is a built-in name, or two installed packages use it;
  • the reader sets no valid file_type.

A reader_format that is neither built in nor an installed plugin is an error when the settings are loaded; the message lists the known formats.
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: In your own scripts
items.text:
Without a package, register a class for the current Python session:

from canvodpy import ReaderFactory, VODFactory

ReaderFactory.register("my_format", MyFormatReader)
VODFactory.register("my_model", MyModel)
reader = ReaderFactory.create(
    "my_format", fpath="ROSA01TUW_R_20250010000_15M_05S_AA.myf"
)

This does not reach canvodpy run, which starts its own Python process; run sees installed plugins only.
path: Your own readers and VOD calculators

items.title: Reference stores
items.text: A reference store is a GNSS store or VOD store built from the test data with a setting profile. New code must reproduce it: a change that alters the stored observations, the satellite geometry or the VOD shows up as a difference when the profiles run again.

items.title: Setting profiles
items.text:
A setting profile is an ordinary settings folder under reference/profiles/. canvodpy run uses it as the settings folder (--config-dir), so the check runs the same code as any run; nothing is patched. Each profile has two files:

  • canvod-settings.yaml: the settings. Data paths are relative to the repository root and point into the test data. The stores name no real person or computer: the identity is the made-up one of the tests, and processing.metadata.record_machine: false leaves the computer out of every commit.
  • reference-runs.yaml: the sites and days the profile runs.

A profile that changes one thing of another profile has only reference-runs.yaml. It names the other profile as base, lists its change under settings and picks sites of the base under sites:

base: default
settings:
  processing:
    params:
      ephemeris_source: broadcast
sites:
  rosalia_sbf: {}    # the base's days and SIDs

Its runs use the base's settings folder; the build merges settings into the settings file it passes with --config. So settings is exactly what differs from the base.

Profile Data Days Settings default both receivers of every site of the test data: Rosalia (RINEX v3.04, SBF, NMEA), MOFLUX (RINEX v2.11), ExampleSite (stripped RINEX v3.05), Hainich (NMEA) 2025-001; Hainich 2026-001 final SP3/CLK from the test data, no preprocessing, SNR only, VOD of each receiver pair, the SIDs of each site (below) sbf-broadcast both receivers of Rosalia (SBF) 2025-001 as default, but the satellite geometry from the broadcast ephemerides the SBF files carry gridded as default as default as default, plus the preprocessing: observations aggregated to 1-minute means (integer flags take the first value of each minute) and assigned to the cells of a 2° equal-area grid

Each site's stores hold that site's own SIDs: per system (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou, the systems the final orbits cover), up to 15 SIDs that both receivers recorded SNR for the longest on the test day. The lists are under sids in reference-runs.yaml. The build writes each site's list into the settings file it passes to that site's run with --config, and a list there replaces the list in canvod-settings.yaml as a whole (see overlay file).

The MOFLUX files carry no receiver position. The build copies them into its output folder with the made-up test position in the header and runs on the copies.

Each store records its site's position in its metadata: the position its data carries, read from the first file of the site's canopy receiver as canvodpy run reads it (for MOFLUX, the made-up test position). The build writes it into the site's settings file, with the address of the published stores (access_url) and the ids of the site's GNSS store and VOD store (related_stores).

A run with a profile downloads nothing: the orbit and clock files come from the test data. The metadata names the made-up identity the tests use, so the stores name no real person. The stores are licensed under Apache 2.0, as the test data.

items.title: Build and check
items.text:
The test data must be checked out (git submodule update --init).

just reference-check                        # run the profiles again and compare with the published stores
just reference-stores ~/reference-stores    # build the stores of every profile into a new folder
just reference-stores ~/broadcast sbf-broadcast   # only the named profiles
just reference-check ~/reference-stores     # compare with a build of your own

just reference-check builds the stores again in a temporary folder and compares each GNSS store and VOD store with the reference stores, using compare_stores (see the store overview). It writes the report to reference-check.txt (empty when the stores match; a second argument sets another path) and exits with 1 on a difference. The reference stores it compares with:

  • without a folder, the published stores: the zips of one commit of the Hugging Face dataset nfb2021/canvodpy-reference-stores named in published.yaml of the folder canvodpy/src/canvodpy/reference-stores/. They are downloaded once into the user cache folder, and each zip's sha256 is checked against SHA256SUMS in the same folder before it is unpacked. The pin is part of the canvodpy package: canvodpy.demo_data("stores") downloads the GNSS and VOD store of the RINEX v3.04 day from it, into a folder of its own, so a demo store written to never changes the reference;
  • a build folder (just reference-stores);
  • a folder of zips (just reference-pack, below).

The folder must hold every profile: the check runs them all.

The published stores were built by canVODpy at commit bd2e6c7b from the test data at commit f0764c4; the card of the dataset lists the profiles and the zips. The DOI of the dataset, doi:10.57967/hf/11189, names its earlier commit ef448847; the pinned commit is 1dea9a15.

For the default profile, a build and a check each take three to four minutes; the SBF day takes the longest. The sbf-broadcast profile takes one and a half minutes, the gridded profile three to four minutes. Two builds of the same code compare with an empty report: the run is deterministic.

items.title: Tolerances
items.text: Integer and flag variables, coordinates, groups, and every attribute except the ones that change with every run (times, ids, the software version; VOLATILE_ATTRIBUTES) must match exactly. Float variables are compared within one absolute tolerance per variable, derived from the finest resolution any format records. The table, with the derivation and its sources, is in the store overview; the code holds it as FLOAT_TOLERANCES in packages/canvod-store/src/canvod/store/comparison.py.

items.title: When the check fails
items.text:
A difference means the new code stores something else. Either the change is a bug, or it is intended: then say so in the pull request, with the report, and change the reference stores (below).

A new setting with a default, or a changed default, fails the check too: the report names it under content_settings. The remedy is the same: new reference stores and a CHANGELOG entry, never an entry in VOLATILE_ATTRIBUTES. That list holds only what changes with every run or release.

items.title: Changing the reference stores
items.text:
1. The pull request says why the stores change and holds the report of just reference-check.
  2. Build every profile from one commit, then pack the build:
just reference-stores ~/reference-stores
just reference-pack ~/reference-stores ~/reference-zips
just reference-check ~/reference-zips    # the zips give an empty report

just reference-pack writes one zip per store, <profile>/<site>-<gnss|vod>.zip, and their sha256 into SHA256SUMS. The zips hold only the stores: no settings files, no logs. It refuses a store that holds a local path (the build folder, the repository, the home folder) or names the computer that packs: its host name, user name or platform. It reads every commit of every branch and refuses one that records the computer (operating system, architecture, CPUs, memory, free disk). The zips are deterministic: packing the same build again gives the same sha256. 3. A maintainer uploads the folder of zips to the Hugging Face dataset:

hf upload nfb2021/canvodpy-reference-stores ~/reference-zips . --repo-type dataset
  1. The pull request moves revision in canvodpy/src/canvodpy/reference-stores/published.yaml to the new commit of the dataset and replaces SHA256SUMS next to it with the new one.

items.title: Stores on S3
items.text:
A run writes its stores into an S3 bucket when processing.storage.stores_root_dir is an s3://bucket/prefix URL (settings file). This page covers what to check before you choose a provider, and how to set up the bucket and the credentials.

Experimental

Stores on S3 are experimental in v1.0.0.

  • Tested against S3 emulators only: the emulator in canVODpy's tests and RustFS. No commercial provider has been tested.
  • The provider must support conditional writes (see Conditional writes). Check this before you choose one.
  • Not everything a local folder offers works on S3 yet: canvodpy store maintain only reports there, and no STAC catalog is written (see Limits).

items.title: Credentials
items.text:
canVODpy reads credentials, region and endpoint only from the environment and the shared AWS files, never from the settings file or the store metadata. They're never logged.

What Where it comes from Access key AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (plus AWS_SESSION_TOKEN for temporary keys), or a profile: AWS_PROFILE and ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.aws/config Region AWS_REGION Endpoint of a provider that isn't AWS AWS_ENDPOINT_URL Bucket in the request path, for self-hosted services such as Ceph CANVOD_S3_PATH_STYLE=1

Give each machine that runs canVODpy its own key, so you can withdraw one machine's access without touching the others.

Temporary credentials must outlast the run

Whether a run renews temporary credentials while it writes hasn't been tested. Until it is, give a run credentials that stay valid longer than the run itself: a backfill of many days can take hours. What a run committed before its credentials expired stays in the store.

items.title: Access policies
items.text:
A run needs to list the store prefix and to read and write objects below it. A run never deletes objects: the commits of a run, and the refusal of a conflicting commit, use only the S3 operations below. This was checked against the S3 emulator with a demo run on S3 that included two runs writing to one store at the same time.

Writer: a machine that runs canVODpy.

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "s3:ListBucket",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::example-bucket",
      "Condition": {"StringLike": {"s3:prefix": "stores/*"}}
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::example-bucket/stores/*"
    }
  ]
}

Reader: someone who opens the stores and reads their data. Use the same policy without s3:PutObject.

Replace example-bucket and stores with your bucket and the prefix of stores_root_dir. Providers other than AWS name these permissions differently or support only part of this policy language; check their documentation.

items.title: Conditional writes
items.text:
Icechunk, the storage engine of the stores, commits with conditional writes: it creates an object only if it doesn't exist yet (If-None-Match) and replaces one only if nobody changed it since it was read (If-Match). This is what keeps two runs that commit to one store at the same time from overwriting each other's commit.

A provider that ignores these conditions accepts both commits, and one of them is lost without an error. Ask the provider whether it supports conditional PUT with If-Match and If-None-Match before you choose it, and don't let two runs write to one store until you know. AWS S3 supports both. On a local folder canVODpy uses a lock file instead, so this question doesn't arise there.

items.title: Bucket settings that break a store
items.text:
A store is many objects that refer to each other. Leave the objects below the store prefix to canVODpy:

  • No lifecycle rule that expires or moves objects below the store prefix. Expiry deletes objects that the store still refers to, and the store can no longer be read. Moving them to an archive storage class makes reads fail until they're restored.
  • No bucket versioning on the store prefix. Icechunk keeps its own history of every commit (snapshots), so versioning adds no safety, and objects deleted by maintenance would stay as old versions you still pay for.
  • Don't delete, rename or copy single objects of a store. To move a store, copy the whole prefix while no run writes to it.

items.title: Costs
items.text: A store on S3 only grows: every commit adds objects, and canvodpy store maintain doesn't delete anything on S3 yet (see Limits). Plan the bucket's size for the full history of every run. canvodpy store maintain SITE --store gnss reports how much maintenance would free.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
These work on a local folder but not yet on S3:

  • canvodpy store maintain and maintain-due only report what they would delete. --execute is refused, because S3 has no lock file that keeps a run from writing during maintenance.
  • No STAC catalog is written for stores on S3.
  • The run history stays in the log folder of the machine that runs, so each machine has its own.
  • Only s3:// URLs: Google Cloud Storage (gs://) and Azure Blob Storage (az://) are refused.

Stores on S3 in the canvod-store-metadata docs shows how to open a store on S3 from Python.

items.title: Settings reference
items.text:
Every setting of canvod-settings.yaml, in the order of the file. For how the file is found and checked, see the Configuration guide.

A name in angle brackets is a name you choose: sites.<site> is a site, <receiver> a receiver and <analysis> a VOD analysis. [] marks a list: each item has the settings listed under it. To print a setting's entry in the terminal, run canvodpy config explain SETTING, for example canvodpy config explain gnss_store.epoch.

ORCID identifier

Your institution or organization name (for example University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences Vienna)

ROR identifier

Department name

Research group name

Institution/group website

items.text:
SPDX license identifier (for example CC-BY-4.0), or other for a license outside SPDX (then license_uri is required). Required when a store is created.

items.text:
URI of the license text; required when license is other

Publisher name. Required when a store is created.

items.text:
Publisher URL

  • Type: text, or null

items.text:
Your institution's domain in reverse order, lowercase (for example org.middle-earth). Required when a store is created: with the store id it gives the store's id in the STAC catalog.

  • Type: text, or null

items.title: processing.metadata.store_description
items.text:
Deprecated: one description for the stores of every site. Use sites.<name>.store_description instead.

  • Type: text, or null

items.title: processing.metadata.initials
items.text:
How a store's metadata records who set its content settings or changed it (for example NFB); the author when not set. Required to amend or migrate a store's metadata.

  • Type: text, or null
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.metadata.record_machine
items.text:
Whether each commit records the computer that writes it: its operating system, architecture, CPU count, memory and free disk. With false they are recorded as null, for stores that are published.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: true

items.title: processing.credentials
items.text: Credentials for external data services

items.title: processing.credentials.nasa_earthdata_acc_mail
items.text:
NASA Earthdata email for CDDIS authentication (optional)

  • Type: email address, or null
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.aux_data
items.text: The orbit and clock products to download

items.title: processing.aux_data.agency
items.text:
Analysis center code

  • Type: text
  • Default: COD

items.title: processing.aux_data.product_type
items.text:
Product type. The agency must publish it: see the product registry of canvod-auxiliary (products.toml).

  • Type: one of final, rapid
  • Default: final

items.title: processing.aux_data.ftp_timeout_s
items.text:
FTP connection timeout in seconds

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: 30

items.title: processing.aux_data.fetch_clock
items.text:
Download and interpolate the CLK clock files with the SP3 orbit files. VOD doesn't use clock corrections, so they are off; set true to add each satellite's clock correction to the GNSS store as the variable clock.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.aux_data.zarr_async_concurrency
items.text:
Limit on Zarr's concurrent chunk reads and writes in the orbit and clock cache; null keeps Zarr's default of 10. Set it when shared_aux_cache_dir is on a network mount (CIFS or NFS) that drops connections during writes.

  • Type: whole number, or null
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.params
items.text: What a run reads and computes, and how many workers it uses

items.title: processing.params.resource_mode
items.text:
auto: OS auto-detects workers and memory (local machines). manual: hard caps via n_max_threads, cpu_affinity and nice_priority (shared servers).

  • Type: one of auto, manual
  • Default: auto

items.title: processing.params.n_max_threads
items.text:
Max worker processes. Required when resource_mode=manual. Ignored in auto.

  • Type: whole number, or null
  • Limits: >= 1, <= 100
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.params.auto_uncapped
items.text:
Remove the automatic CPU core cap of resource_mode auto. On a shared machine, this can starve other users' processes: set it to true only when the machine is yours alone.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.params.keep_gnss_observables
items.text:
GNSS observables to keep (SNR, Pseudorange, Phase, Doppler)

  • Type: list of text
  • Default: ["SNR"]

items.title: processing.params.rinex_v3_parser
items.text:
How RINEX v3 observation files are parsed. validated: every epoch is checked (epoch line, satellite IDs, satellite count, observation fields); epochs that fail are dropped and logged. unvalidated_fast: DANGEROUS. Parses by fixed columns without any check, so corrupted records can enter the store as partial or wrong values. On valid files both give the same dataset. canVODpy takes no responsibility for results of the unvalidated parser; checking the input files is entirely the user's responsibility. Every use emits an UnvalidatedParserWarning.

  • Type: one of validated, unvalidated_fast
  • Default: validated

items.title: processing.params.aggregate_glonass_fdma
items.text:
Aggregate GLONASS FDMA sub-bands into effective G1/G2 bands. When false, the GLONASS signal IDs name the FDMA bands (G1_FDMA, G2_FDMA), for the observations and the orbit data alike. RINEX only: the SBF and NMEA readers refuse false. It changes the GLONASS signal IDs, so an existing store refuses data written with the other value.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: true

items.title: processing.params.store_radial_distance
items.text:
Store radial distance ® in the output store

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.params.store_delta_snr
items.text:
Store delta SNR (SNR_canopy − SNR_reference, dB) in the VOD store. Useful for diagnosing canopy attenuation without the angular correction.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.params.store_radial_diff
items.text:
Store the radial distance difference (r_canopy − r_reference, m) in the VOD store. Requires store_radial_distance: true when the receivers' files are read, so that r is available in both receiver datasets.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.params.receiver_position_mode
items.text:
shared: all receivers use the canopy receiver position for spherical coordinate computation (default, enables 1:1 SNR comparison). per_receiver: each receiver uses its own RINEX header position (physically correct geometry but breaks direct SNR comparability between receivers).

  • Type: one of shared, per_receiver
  • Default: shared

items.title: processing.params.file_pairing
items.text:
complete: discover files per-receiver independently (all data ingested). paired: only process dates where both receivers in an analysis pair have data.

  • Type: one of complete, paired
  • Default: complete

items.title: processing.params.days_per_batch
items.text:
Deprecated: a run derives its days per unit from the memory budget (ADR 0021). If set, a unit has at most this many days.

  • Type: whole number, or null
  • Limits: >= 1, <= 30
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.params.max_memory_gb
items.text:
Memory budget of a run in GB (null = the memory available when the run starts). The run sizes the workers and its days per unit to fit it, and stops before reading a file if not even one worker fits with one day.

  • Type: number, or null
  • Limits: > 0
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.params.cpu_affinity
items.text:
Pin workers to these CPU core IDs (null = no restriction)

  • Type: list of whole number, or null
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.params.nice_priority
items.text:
Priority of the worker processes (-20 = highest, 0 = normal, 19 = lowest). A negative value needs root or CAP_SYS_NICE on Linux; without it, the value has no effect.

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= -20, <= 19
  • Default: -5

items.title: processing.params.threads_per_worker
items.text:
Threads per worker process; null lets the scheduler decide. More than 1 helps array computations and reading and writing, but not the parsing of RINEX text.

  • Type: whole number, or null
  • Limits: >= 1, <= 8
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.params.ephemeris_source
items.text:
final: compute satellite coordinates from agency final products (SP3/CLK). broadcast: use broadcast ephemerides from SBF SatVisibility blocks (SBF reader_format only, skips SP3/CLK download). Broadcast is faster but less accurate (~1-2 m orbit).

  • Type: one of final, broadcast
  • Default: final

items.title: processing.params.store_sbf_raw_observables
items.text:
When reading SBF files, also store the observables before the receiver's corrections: SNR_raw (before CN0HighRes), Pseudorange_unsmoothed (before the Hatch filter), Pseudorange_raw (before the Hatch and multipath filters), and Phase_raw (before the carrier multipath correction). Set to false to make the stores smaller when you don't need them.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: true

items.title: processing.params.store_sbf_metadata
items.text:
When reading SBF files, store each file's SBF metadata (SatVisibility geometry and its almanac or ephemeris source, MeasExtra, PVT, DOP, receiver status and quality indicators) under {group}/metadata/sbf_obs, in the same commit as the observations. Set to false to save space; broadcast geometry (ephemeris_source broadcast) still works, since it uses these data in memory.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: true

Compress the NetCDF files with zlib

Compression level

Zstandard compression level, 0 to 22

Compression algorithm; Icechunk 2 offers only zstd

Chunks up to this size in bytes are stored in the manifest instead of in their own file

Concurrent requests when reading part of a chunk

  • Type: whole number

items.text:
Limit on concurrent storage requests (null = Icechunk's default)

  • Type: whole number, or null

items.text:
Deprecated: has no effect and will be removed with the next major version. It limited Zarr's concurrent chunk writes for only some of the store's writes.

  • Type: whole number, or null
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.icechunk.cache_num_chunk_refs

Number of chunk references Icechunk keeps in memory (null = Icechunk's default)

items.title: processing.icechunk.chunk_strategies
items.text: Chunk shape of each store: a chunk is the piece of an array that is read, compressed, and written as one

items.title: processing.icechunk.chunk_strategies.gnss_store
items.text: Chunks of the GNSS store. A day of ceil(86400 s / cadence) epochs is stored in whole chunks, padded with empty epochs where it does not fill the last one: with 180, days at 1 s, 5 s, 15 s, 30 s or 1 min need no padding, a day at 15 min gets 84 empty epochs.

items.title: processing.icechunk.chunk_strategies.gnss_store.epoch
items.text:
Epochs per chunk, for groups created from now on: a group keeps the chunk size it was created with

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: 180

items.title: processing.icechunk.chunk_strategies.gnss_store.sid
items.text:
Signals per chunk, for groups created from now on; -1 puts all signals in one chunk.

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= -1
  • Default: -1

items.title: processing.icechunk.chunk_strategies.vod_store
items.text: Chunks of the VOD store. As in the GNSS store, each day is stored in whole chunks, padded with empty epochs where it does not fill the last one.

items.title: processing.icechunk.chunk_strategies.vod_store.epoch
items.text:
Epochs per chunk, for groups created from now on: a group keeps the chunk size it was created with

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: 180

items.title: processing.icechunk.chunk_strategies.vod_store.sid
items.text:
Signals per chunk, for groups created from now on; -1 puts all signals in one chunk.

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= -1
  • Default: -1

items.title: processing.icechunk.manifest_preload_enabled
items.text:
Read the manifests of matching arrays when a store is opened

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.icechunk.manifest_preload_max_refs
items.text:
Limit on the chunk references read in advance

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 0
  • Default: 10000

items.title: processing.icechunk.manifest_preload_max_arrays_to_scan
items.text:
Limit on the arrays checked for reading in advance

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: 500

items.title: processing.icechunk.manifest_preload_pattern
items.text:

Enable manifest splitting for stores with large arrays (recommended)

items.title: processing.icechunk.manifest_splitting_epoch_range
items.text:

items.title: processing.storage
items.text: Where the stores are, and what a run does with stored files

items.title: processing.storage.stores_root_dir
items.text:
Folder of the stores: each site's GNSS store and VOD store are under it. A local folder (must exist and be writable) or s3://bucket/prefix (experimental); credentials, region and endpoint of S3 come from the environment.

  • Type: path or text
  • Default: none, you have to set it

items.title: processing.storage.gnss_store_name
items.text:
Folder of the site's GNSS store: gnss, or gnss- and a suffix for a second GNSS store, for example gnss-test. Lowercase letters and digits, with single _ or - between them.

  • Type: text
  • Default: gnss

items.title: processing.storage.vod_store_name
items.text:
Folder of the site's VOD store: vod, or vod- and a suffix for a second VOD store, for example vod-recompute. Lowercase letters and digits, with single _ or - between them.

  • Type: text
  • Default: vod

items.title: processing.storage.aux_data_dir
items.text:
Directory for downloaded auxiliary files (SP3, CLK) and transient Zarr caches. Raw files persist; caches are rebuilt each run. Defaults to system temp directory if not set.

  • Type: path, or null
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.storage.shared_aux_cache_dir
items.text:
Folder of an orbit and clock cache that several sites share (SP3 and CLK, interpolated). null (default): no shared cache; each site's cache is in aux_data_dir and rebuilt every run. Orbit and clock products are the same for every site, so sites that point at the same folder share one cache entry per agency, product and date instead of each building its own.

  • Type: path, or null
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.storage.gnss_store_strategy
items.text:
What a run does with a file that is already in the GNSS store; new files are always written. skip (default): nothing is written. overwrite: the run replaces the file's slots. unsafe_append: kept from versions before day blocks, where it stored the file's epochs twice; it now does what overwrite does.

  • Type: one of skip, overwrite, unsafe_append
  • Default: skip

items.title: processing.storage.vod_store_strategy
items.text:
Deprecated, has no effect. A VOD write skips a result from the same GNSS files as a stored one. Another result replaces the stored VOD of its day. To recompute VOD from the same GNSS files, write to a new VOD store: set vod_store_name to the kind plus a suffix, for example vod-recompute.

  • Type: one of skip, overwrite, unsafe_append, or null
  • Default: null

items.title: processing.storage.keeper_tags
items.text:
Tag every commit of a receiver and day as keep/{receiver}/{yyyydoy}, so a later clean-up can expire everything else. Off by default: the cost of tagging a large store hasn't been measured yet.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.storage.maintenance
items.text: Scheduled clean-up of old snapshots (canvodpy store maintain-due)

items.title: processing.storage.maintenance.enabled
items.text:
Turn on canvodpy store maintain-due. Off by default. Before you turn it on, run garbage_collect(dry_run=True) against your store and check what it would delete.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.storage.maintenance.dry_run_until_confirmed
items.text:
Make every run of canvodpy store maintain-due a dry run until you set this to false. An unattended job can't answer the question that maintain --execute asks; this setting is that answer.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: true

items.title: processing.storage.maintenance.retention_days
items.text:
Days of snapshots the scheduled clean-up keeps; older snapshots are expired and their data collected as garbage. canvodpy store maintain --expire-days, run by hand, doesn't use it.

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 7
  • Default: 90

items.title: processing.storage.maintenance.expire_interval_days
items.text:
Days from one expiration by the scheduled clean-up to the next, counted from the last expiration in the store's operations log.

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: 45

items.title: processing.storage.maintenance.gc_delay_days
items.text:
Days the scheduled clean-up waits after the last expiration before it collects garbage, so it deletes data only some time after their snapshots expired.

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: 20

items.title: processing.storage.maintenance.manifests_enabled
items.text:
Let canvodpy store maintain-due rewrite the manifests, whatever enabled says. A rewrite is an ordinary commit: it changes no history and deletes nothing.

  • Type: true or false
  • Default: false

items.title: processing.storage.maintenance.manifest_count_threshold
items.text:
Number of manifest files in the store at which canvodpy store maintain-due rewrites the manifests.

  • Type: whole number
  • Limits: >= 1
  • Default: 3000

items.title: Upgrading to v1.0.0
items.text:
This page is for everyone who used canVODpy 0.x. Do the four steps before your first run with v1.0.0; the rest of the page lists what changed, what is deprecated and what is new.

Stores written with 0.x must be migrated

A v1.0.0 run refuses a store written by canVODpy 0.x and names the command that migrates it. A nightly run stops there until you migrate. Migrating takes one command per site and keeps every earlier snapshot readable.

items.title: 1. Check the settings file
items.text:
canvodpy config validate

It names every setting that is missing or no longer allowed, with its dotted key. A settings file from 0.x typically needs:

Setting Why processing.logging.log_dir Required for a run: the folder of the log files. processing.metadata.publisher, processing.metadata.license, processing.metadata.naming_authority Required to create a store; the metadata standards (DataCite, STAC) ask for them. sites.<site>.store_description Required to create a store: one sentence about the site's data. processing.metadata.initials Required to migrate or amend a store: who changed its metadata. processing.storage.gnss_store_name, processing.storage.vod_store_name A store's folder is named by its kind (gnss, vod), optionally with a suffix (vod-recompute); other names are refused. Remove gnss_store_name: rinex: the GNSS store's folder is now gnss, and the migration moves it. Remove any other old name too, such as vod_store_name: Site_VOD_store, and move that store with canvodpy store migrate SITE --rename Site_VOD_store=vod; the settings check names the command. processing.preprocessing.temporal_aggregation.integer_method Required when temporal aggregation is set: first, last or middle.

Preprocessing in your settings is now applied

In 0.x, canvodpy run didn't apply processing.preprocessing, and the settings template set temporal_aggregation and grid_assignment to enabled: true. Since v1.0.0 a run applies every preprocessing section that is set. A store you migrate records the preprocessing its data show, none for a store written by canvodpy run in 0.x, and runs with other preprocessing are refused. So if you copied the template, delete the preprocessing section. See Preprocessing.

Settings that are deprecated still work and print a warning that says what to do; they are listed below.

items.title: 2. Back up your stores
items.text: The migration commits to the stores; earlier snapshots stay readable, but keep a copy until you've checked the result. A store is a folder: copy it (cp -a, rsync -a).

items.title: 3. Migrate each site's stores
items.text:
One command per site:

canvodpy store migrate SITE

It shows what it will do, asks once (--yes skips the question), and then takes these steps, skipping each one that is done already:

  1. The folders. A store's folder is named by its kind, gnss or vod, optionally with a suffix (vod-recompute, Store folders). The GNSS store's old folder rinex moves to gnss. Any other folder whose name isn't its kind needs its new name: --rename vod_2024=vod-2024. The store id is taken from the new name. A site that has both rinex and gnss is refused: decide which store to keep. The next steps migrate the stores your settings name (gnss_store_name, vod_store_name). Another store, such as vod-2024, is only moved, and the command says so: to migrate it, set vod_store_name: vod-2024 and run the command again.
  2. The GNSS store, then the VOD store, each with the steps of migrate-metadata and migrate-layout (described below).
  3. The clock. A GNSS store written with CLK files holds a clock variable. v1.0.0 reads no CLK files by default, and VOD doesn't use the clock: the variable is removed and the store records fetch_clock: false. The VOD store records the GNSS store's new content-settings hash, so VOD runs go on.

If a step stops, fix the cause and run the command again. migrate-metadata and migrate-layout run single steps of one store (--store gnss or --store vod):

  • migrate-metadata moves the store to repository metadata: its description, a store id and UUID, the time scale of its epochs, and its content settings, the settings that shape its data and that every later run must match (Content settings). Metadata the store lacks, such as the publisher and license, comes from the settings file, marked (from the settings). A store that is already migrated is left as it is.
  • migrate-layout writes the groups again as day blocks, the layout v1.0.0 runs write (Moving a store to day blocks). An epoch stored twice keeps the entry written last.

Both show what they change and ask first. Each one is a single commit. The details are in Move an older store to the current form.

Settings the store doesn't record. migrate-metadata takes the content settings from the settings recorded in the store's first commit. A value that commit doesn't record isn't guessed: the command stops, lists it, and you give it with --gnss-set (or --vod-set for the VOD store), as your settings file had it when the store was written. For a GNSS store from canVODpy 0.4.0 these are typically:

canvodpy store migrate SITE \
  --gnss-set processing.params.store_sbf_metadata=true \
  --gnss-set processing.params.rinex_v3_parser=validated \
  --gnss-set "sites.SITE.receivers.reference_01.paired_canopies=[canopy_01]"

Some settings are read from the data instead, because canVODpy 0.x recorded settings its runs didn't follow: the preprocessing (none, unless the data show a step) and whether the stores hold r, delta_snr and radial_diff. canVODpy 0.x always wrote delta_snr to the VOD store, so a migrated store records store_delta_snr: true: set it in your settings file too.

Stores from SBF or NMEA files. canVODpy 0.x stored their epochs in UTC, 18 s behind the GPS time v1.0.0 uses for every epoch. The migration refuses these stores before it writes anything, and so does the VOD store computed from them: rebuild them from the raw files with canvodpy run. Stores from RINEX files hold GPS time and migrate as they are.

Receivers with a naming recipe. A GNSS store records each receiver's naming recipe and the sha256 of the recipe file, and every run compares them with the settings. Stores of canVODpy 0.x record the recipe, if the receiver had one, without its sha256; a receiver that used the naming block and now has a recipe records none. The migration doesn't add them: it can't tell whether today's recipe file is the one the store was built with. For each receiver with a naming recipe, check that its recipe file is the one the store was built with, then record it:

canvodpy store amend SITE --store gnss --update-recipe RECEIVER \
    --reason "recipe of the stored days, recorded after the migration"

Without this, the first run stops and prints the command. Sites whose files have canonical canVOD names have no recipes and skip this.

items.title: 4. Check the result
items.text:
canvodpy store info SITE            # content settings: set, with their hash
canvodpy run --site SITE --start 2025001 --end 2025001

A run compares your settings with the store's content settings before it reads a file, and stops if they differ, listing each setting with both values. Change your settings to the store's values, or write a settings file from the store with canvodpy config init --from-store <store>. A dry run (--dry-run) lists the files a run would process, but doesn't compare the settings.

items.title: What changed
items.text: Before (0.x) Since v1.0.0 What to do Runs append each file to the store. Runs write day blocks: every receiver-day has its slots, and a day processed again replaces its slots (ADR 0016). Migrate the stores (step 3). A store had no fixed settings. A store records its content settings when it is created; a run with other settings is refused (ADR 0019). To process with other settings, write a new store (gnss_store_name: gnss-<suffix>). Opening a store created it. Only a run creates a store; open_gnss_store() and open_vod_store() only open. Create stores with canvodpy run. A store's site came from its folder name. It comes from the store's metadata. Nothing; migrated stores have it. The GNSS store's folder was rinex, and store folders could have any name. A store's folder is named by its kind: gnss, vod, or the kind with a suffix (Store folders); the store id ends in it. Migrate the stores (step 3); the migration moves rinex to gnss. canvodpy run without dates resumed from the last stored day. A run without dates stops. --update-to-latest processes the days from the earliest last stored day of the receivers with new files up to the latest day with files (Which days a run processes). Add --update-to-latest to scheduled runs. processing.preprocessing had no effect. A run applies each section that is set. See the warning in step 1. Files were found in day folders with fixed names. Each file's day comes from its name, in any folder layout. Nothing; files with other names need a naming recipe (File names). max_memory_gb was a memory limit a run checked while it worked. It is the run's memory budget, applied before the work starts: it sizes the workers and the units of days a run commits at once (Parallel processing). Check its value. A run computed the VOD of each day in the main process, from the day read back from the GNSS store, and committed the VOD store every day. A run stores a unit of days, then computes their VOD in the worker processes from the GNSS store and commits the VOD store once per unit (ADR 0021). Nothing is read back for VOD. In Python, pipeline.run() does what canvodpy run does. The Airflow task process_day returns the groups that stored the day, no longer their number of epochs. Use pipeline.run() instead of process_range() with site.vod.compute_day_all() to process and compute VOD. A run processed days_per_batch days at a time and committed every day. A run works in units of days and commits each unit once; it sizes the units from the memory budget, at most 31 days (ADR 0021). A day that fails still fails alone. Remove days_per_batch (deprecated). A store recorded the name of each receiver's naming recipe. A GNSS store records each receiver's naming recipe and the sha256 of its file; a run stops if the settings give another recipe, or the recipe file changed (File names). Record the recipes after migrating (step 3). After changing a recipe on purpose, canvodpy store amend SITE --store gnss --update-recipe RECEIVER --reason "...". canvodpy[filemap] installed canvod-filemap. The extra is gone. Install canvod-filemap from its tag (Optional extensions), or uv sync --group filemap in the repository. canvod-grids installed canvod-store and canvod-store-metadata. It doesn't. Code that imports canvod.store declares canvod-store itself.

items.title: New in v1.0.0
items.text:
• Stores on S3, experimental: runs write GNSS and VOD stores to S3-compatible object storage, tested against S3 emulators only (Stores on S3).
  • Store metadata after DataCite and ACDD, checked against the standards, and a STAC catalog of all stores (canvodpy run --write-catalog; Store metadata).
  • Settings from a link: --config-dir and CANVOD_CONFIG_DIR take the raw GitHub link of a settings file; naming recipes are read from the same repository (Settings from a GitHub repository).
  • Join or reproduce a store: canvodpy config init --from-store writes the settings file of a store (Settings file).
  • Run history and dashboard: every run records itself, its stage timings and resource use (Diagnostics and monitoring).
  • Data check: canvodpy config validate checks the receiver data the way a run finds it, and runs warn about files they don't process and about incomplete receiver-days.
  • Memory budget and units of days: max_memory_gb sizes the workers and the units of days a run commits at once, and a run reads the next unit while it computes VOD (Parallel processing).
  • A complete command line: canvodpy run, vod, vod-reconcile, config, store, stac, doctor and dashboard (Command line).
  • Plugins: your own readers and VOD calculators from installed packages (Your own readers and VOD calculators).
  • Comparing stores within fixed tolerances, and canvodpy config explain.
  • Stores that don't record the computer: processing.metadata.record_machine: false leaves the operating system, architecture, CPU count, memory and free disk out of every commit, for stores that are published (Settings). It is true by default, so nothing changes for you.
  • Demo data: canvodpy.demo_data() downloads the demo day; the notebooks use it.

The full list is in the changelog.

items.title: Coordinate systems
items.text:
canvod-auxiliary works with three coordinate systems. Knowing which one is used where prevents sign errors and unit confusion in downstream VOD calculations.

  • ECEF

    Earth-Centered, Earth-Fixed Cartesian (X, Y, Z) in meters. Used in SP3 ephemerides and the internal satellite position pipeline.

  • Geodetic (WGS84)

    Latitude, longitude (degrees), altitude above ellipsoid (meters). Stored in RINEX headers as the approximate receiver position.

  • Spherical (receiver-relative)

    Slant range \(r\), polar angle \(\theta\), geographic azimuth \(\varphi\). This is the output added to the obs Dataset for VOD geometry.

items.title: ECEF coordinates
items.text:
Satellite positions from SP3 files are ECEF Cartesian coordinates in meters, one position per satellite and epoch.

from canvod.auxiliary import ECEFPosition

# From raw values
ecef = ECEFPosition(x=4_075_539.8, y=931_735.3, z=4_801_629.6)

# From RINEX Dataset metadata (reads APPROX POSITION header)
ecef = ECEFPosition.from_ds_metadata(rinex_ds)

# Convert to geodetic
lat, lon, alt = ecef.to_geodetic()

items.title: Geodetic coordinates
items.text:
WGS84 geodetic coordinates for the receiver position, read from the APPROX POSITION XYZ RINEX header field.

from canvod.auxiliary import GeodeticPosition

geo = GeodeticPosition(lat=48.2, lon=16.4, alt=200.0)

# Convert to ECEF for vector calculations
ecef = geo.to_ecef()  # ECEFPosition

items.title: Spherical coordinates (receiver-relative)
items.text:
The key output of the auxiliary pipeline, added to the obs Dataset as theta and phi coordinates for each (epoch, sid) cell.

Variable Symbol Range Convention Slant range \(r\) \(\geq 0\) m Distance from receiver antenna to satellite Polar angle \(\theta\) \([0, \pi/2]\) 0 = overhead (zenith), \(\pi/2\) = horizon Geographic azimuth \(\varphi\) \([0, 2\pi)\) 0 = North, \(\pi/2\) = East, clockwise

All three are NaN while the satellite is below the receiver's horizon.

Polar angle vs elevation

VOD literature often uses elevation angle \(e = \pi/2 - \theta\). canvod-auxiliary stores polar angle \(\theta\) internally. The \(\cos\theta\) factor in the tau-omega formula uses \(\theta\) directly: \(\text{VOD} = -\ln(T) \cdot \cos\theta\).

items.title: Computing spherical coordinates
items.text:
from canvod.auxiliary import compute_spherical_coordinates

r, theta, phi = compute_spherical_coordinates(
    # satellite ECEF positions, arrays of any shape
    sat_x,
    sat_y,
    sat_z,
    receiver_position,  # ECEFPosition
)

The function:

  1. Subtracts the receiver ECEF position from each satellite ECEF position.
  2. Rotates the difference vector into the local ENU (East-North-Up) frame.
  3. Converts ENU to spherical \((r, \theta, \varphi)\) and sets all three to NaN below the horizon.

items.title: Adding coordinates to datasets
items.text:
In a run the interpolated satellite positions are first selected for each signal, so \((r, \theta, \varphi)\) come out on (epoch, sid) and are attached to the observation dataset:

from canvod.auxiliary import add_spherical_coords_to_dataset

augmented_ds = add_spherical_coords_to_dataset(rinex_ds, r, theta, phi)

# New data variables on (epoch, sid):
# augmented_ds["theta"]   → polar angle [rad]
# augmented_ds["phi"]     → geographic azimuth [rad]
# augmented_ds["r"]       → slant range [m]

A run keeps r only when processing.params.store_radial_distance is true (default false).

items.title: Interpolation methods
items.text:
SP3 orbits come every 5 or 15 minutes and CLK clocks every 30 s or 5 minutes; observations come every 1 to 30 s. canvod-auxiliary interpolates one day of orbits and clocks onto a regular grid that starts at 00:00 and has the sampling interval of the observations (canvod.auxiliary.interpolation.interpolate_aux_day). Each observation epoch then takes the nearest grid epoch. canvodpy run, the ephemeris provider of the Python API and the Airflow tasks all use these functions.

  • Cubic Hermite spline

    Used for SP3 orbits (satellite X, Y, Z).

    The spline matches the positions and the satellite velocities at every SP3 epoch.

  • Piecewise linear

    Used for CLK clock offsets.

    Linear between neighboring clock epochs, never across a detected clock jump.

items.title: Cubic Hermite spline (orbits)
items.text:
Orbital motion is smooth, so a cubic polynomial between two SP3 epochs fits it well. A Hermite spline fixes each polynomial by the positions and velocities at both ends of the interval (scipy.interpolate.CubicHermiteSpline).

SP3 files read by canVODpy provide positions only. The SP3 reader (Sp3File, add_velocities=True by default) estimates the velocities from the positions by central differences (forward and backward differences at the first and last epoch); a run computes them on the day joined with its neighbors (see below), so the day's own first and last epochs get central differences too.

from canvod.auxiliary.interpolation import Sp3Config, Sp3InterpolationStrategy

config = Sp3Config(
    use_velocities=True,  # Hermite spline with Vx, Vy, Vz
    fallback_method="linear",  # used when the dataset has no velocities
)

interpolator = Sp3InterpolationStrategy(config=config)
result = interpolator.interpolate(sp3_data, target_epochs)
Parameter Default Effect use_velocities True Hermite spline if Vx, Vy, Vz are in the dataset fallback_method "linear" xarray interpolation method without velocities

items.title: Start and end of the day
items.text:
A daily orbit file can end before midnight (ESA's 15-minute rapid orbits end at 23:45; CODE's 5-minute orbits include 24:00), and the velocities of its first and last epoch are one-sided differences. So every run loads the orbit and clock files of the previous and the next day too (AuxDataPipeline.create_standard), keeps one hour of each (AuxFile.join_days; where files overlap, the day's own epoch is kept) and computes the velocities on the joined data. Every epoch of the day then lies between two orbit epochs: nothing is extrapolated. If a neighboring day's file cannot be obtained, the run stops with an error naming it. Final products come out per GPS week, so the last day of a week can be processed only once the next week's products are published.

The spline is fitted per satellite on the epochs with data. A target epoch outside a satellite's data, or in a gap of more than 1.5 sampling intervals, is NaN.

items.title: Accuracy
items.text:
Measured on the CODE final orbits of 2025-001 (with 2024-366 and 2025-002), by leaving orbit epochs out and interpolating them from the rest; the angle is the largest direction error seen from the ground:

Orbit sampling Largest position error Largest angle error 10 min (positions at the 5-min epochs in between) 81 m \(0.0002^\circ\) 15 min 1.1 km \(0.004^\circ\)

With the day's file alone (before the neighbors were loaded), the first and last interval of the day were off by up to 37 km (\(0.11^\circ\)), and a 15-minute file ending at 23:45 was extrapolated by up to 990 km (\(2.9^\circ\)).

items.title: Piecewise linear (clocks)
items.text:
Satellite clock offsets can jump. Linear interpolation between neighboring CLK epochs, split at each jump, avoids fitting across one.

from canvod.auxiliary.interpolation import ClockConfig, ClockInterpolationStrategy

config = ClockConfig(
    window_size=9,  # epochs averaged on each side of a candidate jump
    jump_threshold=1e-6,  # jump detection threshold (seconds)
)

interpolator = ClockInterpolationStrategy(config=config)
result = interpolator.interpolate(clk_data, target_epochs)

Jump detection

For each gap between consecutive CLK epochs, the interpolator compares the mean of up to window_size epochs before the gap with the mean of up to window_size epochs after it. Where the difference exceeds jump_threshold, the gap is a jump (for a run of flagged gaps, only the one with the largest difference). The series is split at each jump and interpolated linearly within each segment, never across a jump. Target epochs inside a jump gap, outside the data, or in a segment of a single epoch are NaN. window_size=1 compares the two neighboring epochs only.

The strategy interpolates every data variable whose name contains clock, clk, Clock or CLK, and raises ValueError if there is none.

items.title: Recorded in the data
items.text: interpolate_aux_day writes the class and settings of each strategy to the interpolated orbits and clocks (attrs["interpolator_config"], from Interpolator.to_attrs()), and create_interpolator_from_attrs() rebuilds the interpolator from these attributes.

items.title: Custom strategies
items.text:
Subclass Interpolator to write your own interpolation:

import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
from canvod.auxiliary.interpolation import Interpolator


class CustomStrategy(Interpolator):
    """Example: Lagrange polynomial interpolation."""

    def interpolate(
        self,
        ds: xr.Dataset,
        target_epochs: np.ndarray,
    ) -> xr.Dataset:
        # Your implementation here
        return interpolated_ds

canvodpy run always uses Sp3InterpolationStrategy and ClockInterpolationStrategy; a custom strategy is for your own scripts.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: The canvod-auxiliary package provides auxiliary data management for GNSS Transmissometry (GNSS-T) analysis. It handles downloading, parsing, preprocessing, and interpolating SP3 ephemerides to augment RINEX observation data with precise satellite positions. It can also fetch CLK clock corrections with aux_data.fetch_clock: true; the VOD formula doesn't use them, so they are off by default.

items.title: The dimension alignment problem
items.text:
GNSS-T analysis requires combining two data sources with fundamentally different indexing:

RINEX Observations

  • High temporal resolution: 30 s, 15 s, or sub-second
  • Signal-level indexing by SID: "G01|L1|C"
  • Dimensions: (epoch: 2880, sid: 384)

SP3 / CLK Auxiliary

  • Low temporal resolution: 5–15 min
  • Satellite-level indexing by SV: "G01"
  • Dimensions: (epoch: 96, sv: 32)
  • CLK is optional (aux_data.fetch_clock, default false); SP3 is always required

Combining these requires:

  1. Dimension conversion from sv (32 satellites) to sid (384 signal IDs)
  2. Temporal interpolation from 15 min to the observations' sampling interval, on a grid from 00:00
  3. Coordinate transform from ECEF to geodetic to spherical \((r, \theta, \varphi)\)
  4. Physically correct interpolation per data type
graph TD
    A["`**SP3 File**
    sv dimension`"]
    A -->|Download| B["`**Raw Dataset**
    96 epochs, 32 svs`"]
    B -->|Preprocess| C["`**Preprocessed**
    96 epochs, 384 sids`"]
    C -->|Interpolate| D["`**Interpolated**
    2880 epochs, 384 sids`"]
    D -->|Augment| E["`**RINEX Dataset**
    2880 epochs, 384 sids`"]

items.title: Interpolation strategies
items.text:
Different data types require different methods based on the underlying physics:

  • SP3 (Hermite cubic splines)

    Satellite orbital motion is smooth and predictable. Hermite splines exploit available velocity data for C1-continuity and sub-millimeter interpolation accuracy.

    config = Sp3Config(use_velocities=True, fallback="linear")
strategy = Sp3InterpolationStrategy(config=config)

  • CLK (piecewise linear)

    Clock corrections may have discontinuities from satellite maneuvers and uploads. No derivative information is available. Piecewise linear interpolation handles these jumps safely.

    config = ClkConfig(window_size=9, jump_threshold=1e-6)
strategy = ClockInterpolationStrategy(config=config)

items.title: Key components
items.text:
• File Handlers

    Sp3File reads SP3a/c/d files: positions (X, Y, Z) and velocities (VX, VY, VZ)

    ClkFile reads RINEX clock files: satellite clock biases

    ProductSpec describes a product: its URLs, latency, and authentication

  • Preprocessing

    prep_aux_ds() runs four steps: map sv to sid, pad to the global SIDs, normalize the dtype, strip _FillValue

    sp3_sid = prep_aux_ds(sp3_raw)
# {'epoch': 96, 'sid': 384}

  • Coordinate Classes

    ECEFPosition holds Earth-Centered Earth-Fixed (X, Y, Z)

    GeodeticPosition holds WGS84 latitude, longitude, and altitude

    Spherical coordinates \((r, \theta, \varphi)\) relative to receiver position

  • FTP Download

    Without a NASA Earthdata account, from ESA GSSC only

    With one, from NASA CDDIS first and from ESA GSSC if that fails

    Per-DOY caching prevents redundant downloads

items.title: Usage
items.text:
Add satellite geometry to a datasetData flow

In a run, an ephemeris provider does every step below; use it the same way in your own code:

from canvod.auxiliary import ECEFPosition
from canvod.auxiliary.ephemeris.provider import AgencyEphemerisProvider
from canvod.config import load_config
from canvod.readers import Rnxv3Obs

site_config = load_config().sites.sites["ExampleSite"]
ds = Rnxv3Obs(fpath="ROSA01TUW_R_20250010000_01D_05S_AA.rnx").to_ds()

provider = AgencyEphemerisProvider(agency="COD", product_type="final", fetch_clock=True)
provider.preprocess_day("2025001", site_config)  # download and read SP3 (and CLK)
augmented = provider.augment_dataset(ds, ECEFPosition.from_ds_metadata(ds))
# augmented has theta and phi (radians) on (epoch, sid)

augment_dataset interpolates the day once onto the epoch grid (00:00 plus multiples of the dataset's sampling interval, canvod.auxiliary.interpolation.day_grid), caches it, gives each observation the nearest grid epoch and converts ECEF positions to \(\theta\), \(\varphi\) relative to the receiver position from the data.

sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Sp3File
    participant Preprocessor
    participant Interpolator
    participant Coordinates

    User->>Sp3File: Sp3File(date, agency, product_type, ...)
    Sp3File->>Sp3File: FTP download + parse
    Sp3File-->>User: to_dataset() {epoch: 96, sv: 32}

    User->>Preprocessor: prep_aux_ds(sp3_raw)
    Preprocessor-->>User: {epoch: 96, sid: 384}

    User->>Interpolator: interpolate onto the day's epoch grid
    Interpolator->>Interpolator: Hermite splines
    Interpolator-->>User: {epoch: 2880, sid: 384}

    User->>Coordinates: compute_spherical_coordinates()
    Coordinates-->>User: (r, θ, φ) arrays

    User->>User: add_spherical_coords_to_dataset()

items.title: Preprocessing pipeline
items.text:
Before interpolation, auxiliary data must be restructured to match the (epoch × sid) layout of the observation datasets. This pipeline bridges the sv (satellite) indexing of SP3/CLK files and the sid (signal ID) indexing of the observations.

In a run, AuxDataPipeline calls prep_aux_ds() with the signal IDs kept by the sids: settings, so the orbits and clocks carry the same signals as the observations before they are interpolated.

items.title: The dimension mismatch problem
items.text:
SP3 / CLK files

Index by satellite vehicle (sv):

sp3_data.dims
# {'epoch': 96, 'sv': 32}

GPS G01 has one entry: one position per epoch.

RINEX obs Dataset

Index by signal ID (sid):

rinex_data.dims
# {'epoch': 2880, 'sid': 384}

GPS G01 maps to up to 28 Signal IDs (L1C, L2W, L5Q, …).

Satellite position is frequency-independent (all signals leave the same antenna), so the sv \(\rightarrow\) sid mapping simply replicates each position across all signal IDs for that satellite.

items.title: Pipeline functions
